summary: Police informer Juan Rull, who with his family had set off bombs in Barcelona for years and collected fees from police for fake information, was arrested, producing a scandal.

citation.quote: Rull's arrest in July 1907 produced a scandal that lingered beyond his execution in August, a year later.

title: Founding of Solidaridad Obrera
summary: Solidaridad Obrera (Worker Solidarity) was founded as a municipal federation in Barcelona; two months later it began publishing a newspaper of the same name.

citation.quote: The federation, called Solidaridad Obrera (Worker Solidarity), was founded on August 3 and two months later began publishing a newspaper of the same name.

title: Anarchist Congress at Amsterdam
summary: The Congres Anarchiste is held in Amsterdam from August 24-31, 1907, featuring Errico Malatesta's criticisms of syndicalism (proceedings later published in Paris, 1908).

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Errico Malatesta's criticisms of syndicalism appear in the *Compte Rendu Analytique* of the *Congres Anarchiste Tenu a Amsterdam, Aout 24–31, 1907* (Paris, 1908).

title: Death of Fermin Salvochea
summary: Fermin Salvochea died in Cadiz, the gleaming white city he loved so dearly. Fifty thousand people followed in the cortege to the cemetery, raising a spontaneous cry of 'Viva la anarquia!'

citation.quote: On September 8, 1907, Fermin Salvochea died in Cadiz, the gleaming white city he loved so dearly.

title: Sorel publishes Reflexions sur la Violence
summary: Georges Sorel's Reflexions sur la Violence is originally published in Paris.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: The impact of Georges Sorel's *Reflexions sur la Violence* (originally published in Paris, 1908, and easily available in English translation) has been greatly overrated

title: Execution of Juan Rull
summary: Police informer Juan Rull was executed in Barcelona, a year after his arrest. On the day of his execution a bomb exploded on a main boulevard with a note claiming Rull's innocence.

citation.quote: Rull's arrest in July 1907 produced a scandal that lingered beyond his execution in August, a year later. On that day, a bomb went off on a main boulevard of Barcelona.

title: Solidaridad Obrera expands into regional federation
summary: Solidaridad Obrera was expanded into a regional federation embracing 112 labor syndicates throughout Catalonia with a membership of twenty-five thousand workers.

citation.quote: A year later, in September 1908, it was expanded into a regional federation embracing 112 labor syndicates throughout Catalonia with a membership of twenty five thousand workers.

title: Riera publishes La Semana Tragica
summary: Augusto Riera's La Semana Tragica is published in Barcelona, presenting the conventional attitude toward the Tragic Week with photographs and inventories.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: The conventional attitude toward the "Tragic Week" appears in Augusto Riera's *La Semana Tragica* (Barcelona, 1909)

title: McCabe publishes The Martyrdom of Ferrer
summary: Joseph McCabe's The Martyrdom of Ferrer is published in London shortly after Ferrer's execution, reflecting the worldwide impact of the Spanish educator.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: McCabe's *The Martyrdom of Ferrer* (London, 1909), both of which appeared shortly after Ferrer's execution and reflect the worldwide impact of the Spanish educator.

title: Lerroux goes abroad to escape sedition trial
summary: Alejandro Lerroux went abroad to escape trial on an old charge of writing a seditious article, remaining away until October 1909, after the Tragic Week upheaval had subsided.

citation.quote: Lerroux had gone abroad in February 1909 to escape trial on an old charge of writing a seditious article. He prudently remained away until October 1909, long after the upheaval had subsided.

title: Rusinol factory lockout in Ter valley
summary: The Rusinol factory in the Ter valley was closed down and 800 workers discharged, opening a campaign to lower wages throughout the Catalan textile industry.

citation.quote: On May 15, the Rusinol factory in the Ter valley was closed down, and 800 workers were discharged. The lockout was the opening blow in another campaign to lower wages throughout the textile industry.

title: Solidaridad Obrera congress accepts general strike tactic
summary: A congress of the Solidaridad Obrera labor federation voted overwhelmingly to accept the general strike tactic “depending upon circumstances,” marking the success of Anarchosyndicalist influence.

citation.quote: The periodical *Solidaridad Obrera* soon fell under Anarchosyndicalist control and on June 13, 1909, a congress of the labor federation voted overwhelmingly to accept the general strike tactic “depending upon circumstances.”

title: Maura ministry calls up military reserves for Morocco
summary: The Maura ministry announced a call-up of military reserves for active duty in Morocco amid skirmishes between Riff tribesmen and Spanish troops, producing heartrending scenes in Barcelona.

citation.quote: It was against this background of mounting crisis in Barcelona that the Maura ministry, on July 11, announced a call-up of military reserves for active duty in Morocco.

title: Pablo Iglesias warns of general strike at Madrid rally
summary: Pablo Iglesias warned an antiwar rally in Madrid that “if it is necessary, workers will go out on a general strike with all the consequences.”

citation.quote: On July 18, Pablo Iglesias, a man who for decades had made prudence the keystone of Socialist policy, warned an antiwar rally in Madrid that “if it is necessary, workers will go out on a general strike with all the consequences.”

title: El Poble Catala publishes Socialist petition for general strike
summary: El Poble Catala published a petition by the Catalan Socialists to their Madrid headquarters calling for a general strike throughout Spain, raising the crisis in Barcelona to acute dimensions.

citation.quote: This crisis was raised to acute dimensions in Barcelona when on July 21 *El Poble Catala* published a petition by the Catalan Socialists to their Madrid headquarters, calling for a general strike throughout Spain.

title: Formation of Central Committee for a Strike
summary: Two Barcelona Anarchists, Jose Rodriguez Romero and Miguel Villalobos Morena, constituted themselves as the nucleus of a Central Committee for a Strike on Saturday night.

citation.quote: The stalemate was suddenly broken on the night of July 24, when two Barcelona Anarchists, Jose Rodriguez Romero and Miguel Villalobos Morena, decided to constitute themselves as the nucleus of a Central Committee for a strike.

title: The Tragic Week insurrection in Barcelona
summary: During the week of July 26 to August 1, Barcelona presented the spectacle of a full-scale insurrection, a largely spontaneous uprising with barricades, attacks on police, and the burning of an estimated eighty churches and monasteries.

citation.quote: During the week of July 26 to August 1, Barcelona would present the spectacle of a full-scale insurrection, a largely spontaneous uprising that received little guidance from the union or Radical leaders.

title: UGT issues belated general strike appeal
summary: The UGT, the only national labor federation in Spain at the time, did not issue an appeal for a general strike until Tuesday night, July 27, scheduling the strike for August 2 — two days after the Barcelona insurrection had been suppressed.

citation.quote: For instance, the UGT, the only national labor federation in Spain at the time, did not issue an appeal for a general strike until Tuesday night, July 27, two days after Barcelona had risen.

title: Troops deployed against Barcelona insurrectionaries
summary: Large troop detachments reached Barcelona on Wednesday, July 28, and were deployed against the insurrectionaries; artillery was needed to clear barricades in the Clot and Pueblo Nueva districts.

citation.quote: By Wednesday, July 28, large troop detachments reached the city and were deployed against the insurrectionaries. Intense fighting continued well into the next day.

title: End of fighting in Barcelona at Horta
summary: The fighting in Barcelona came to an end on Saturday, July 31, when Horta, the last outpost of rebel resistance, was overcome.

citation.quote: The fighting in Barcelona came to an end on Saturday, July 31, when Horta, the last outpost of rebel resistance, was overcome.

title: Francisco Ferrer captured
summary: Francisco Ferrer was captured on August 31, 1909, after hiding for five weeks in caves on his farm; the prelates of Barcelona then sent a letter to Maura demanding vigorous action against him.

citation.quote: When he was captured on August 31, after hiding for five weeks in caves on his farm, the prelates of Barcelona sent a letter to Maura openly demanding vigorous action against Ferrer and the *Escuela Moderna.*

title: Execution of Francisco Ferrer at Montjuich
summary: Francisco Ferrer was executed by a firing squad in Montjuich prison after a one-day military trial; his last words were “Look well, my children! I am innocent. Long live the Escuela Moderna!”

citation.quote: On the morning of October 13, 1909, Ferrer was executed by a firing squad in Montjuich prison. He is said to have died serenely and with great courage.

title: Moret replaces Maura as premier
summary: The Liberal Moret replaced Maura as premier, publicly committed to a less repressive program after an alliance with the Republicans to unseat the ministry.

citation.quote: When the Liberal Moret replaced Maura as premier on October 21, 1909, he was publicly committed to a less repressive program.

title: Tragic Week Anarchists transferred to civilian courts
summary: Four Anarchists charged with rebellion in the 'Tragic Week' were removed from military jurisdiction and turned over to civilian courts; days later martial law was lifted in Catalonia and a general amnesty declared.

citation.quote: In November, four Anarchists charged with rebellion in the "Tragic Week" were removed from military jurisdiction and turned over to civilian courts. A few days later, martial law was lifted in Catalonia.

title: Civil rule restored in Catalonia
summary: Full civil rule was not restored in Catalonia until November 7, almost six weeks after its restoration in the rest of Spain, following the post-Tragic Week repression.

citation.quote: Although Spain had been placed under martial law directly after the outbreak of the insurrection, full civil rule was not restored in Catalonia until November 7, almost six weeks after its restoration in the rest of the country.

title: Solidaridad Obrera holds reorganizing assembly
summary: Solidaridad Obrera held a special assembly to piece the organization back together, attended by delegates from only twenty-seven unions—a substantial decline from the 108 represented eight months earlier.

citation.quote: On December 18,1909, Solidaridad Obrera held a special assembly to piece the organization back together.

title: Founding meeting of the CNT in Barcelona
summary: Delegates from local confederations throughout Spain convened at the Palacio de Bellas Artes in Barcelona, where the decision was made to establish the National Confederation of Labor (CNT).

citation.quote: On October 30, 1910, delegates from local confederations throughout Spain convened at the Palacio de Bellas Artes in Barcelona for an informal three-day exchange of views and experiences.

title: First congress of the CNT
summary: The CNT's first congress was held at the Bellas Artes in Barcelona between September 8 and 11, 1911. Delegates represented some 30,000 members in 350 unions throughout Spain.

citation.quote: The movement really got underway at the CNT's first congress, also held in the Bellas Artes, between September 8 and 11 of 1911.

title: Barcelona police round up CNT militants
summary: On the night of September 15, Barcelona police rounded up five hundred CNT militants and, with the cooperation of Lerroux, managed to stop the planned strike movement in the city.

citation.quote: On the night of September 15, the Barcelona police rounded up five hundred CNT militants or cenetistas (as members of the organization were soon to be called) and, with the cooperation of Lerroux, who regarded the union as a rival of the Radicals, managed to stop the strike movement.

title: CNT general strike and Cullera uprising
summary: A general strike scheduled by the CNT spread from Saragossa to Gijon, Valencia, and Seville. In Cullera, near Valencia, the strike exploded into full-scale insurrection during which the mayor and a judge were killed.

citation.quote: The action was scheduled for September 16—only five days after the founding of the CNT. The general strike started in Saragossa and spread rapidly to Gijon, Valencia, and Seville.

title: Canalejas drafts railway strikers into the army
summary: To break a railway strike in 1912, Liberal premier Canalejas drafted 12,000 of the workers into the army.

citation.quote: To break a railway strike in 1912, Canalejas drafted 12,000 of the workers into the army.

title: Assassination of premier Canalejas
summary: Liberal premier Canalejas was shot to death in the Puerta del Sol, the main plaza of Madrid, by a young Aragonese Anarchist, Miguel Pardinas, who then took his own life.

citation.quote: He was shot to death in the Puerta del Sol, the main plaza of Madrid, by a young Aragonese Anarchist, Miguel Pardinas.

title: Death sentences for Cullera uprising Anarchists
summary: Five Anarchists were given death sentences for their part in the Cullera uprising, but these were commuted to life imprisonment. Juan Jover Ferrer was spared the garrot by Alfonso XIII.

citation.quote: On January 10, 1912, five Anarchists were given death sentences for their part in the Cullera uprising, but these were commuted to life imprisonment.

title: Romanones declares amnesty for September 1911 strikers
summary: In 1913, Canalejas's successor, the Liberal premier Romanones, declared an amnesty for all imprisoned offenders in the general strike of September 1911, though the CNT remained illegal.

citation.quote: In 1913, Canalejas's successor, the Liberal premier Romanones, declared an amnesty for all imprisoned offenders in the general strike of September 1911.

title: Federation National de Agricultores founded at Cordoba congress
summary: A congress at Cordoba led to the founding of the Federation National de Agricultores (FNA), which won most of Murcia and Valencia to the libertarian fold before dissolving into the CNT in 1919.

citation.quote: Signs of a recovery were already evident in the spring of 1913, when a congress at Cordoba had led to the founding of the Federation National de Agricultores (FNA).

title: McCabe translates Ferrer's The Origin and Ideas of the Modern School
summary: Ferrer's La Escuela Moderna is translated into English by Joseph McCabe under the title The Origin and Ideas of the Modern School, published in London.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Ferrer's *La Escuela Moderna* has been translated into English by Joseph McCabe under the title, *The Origin and Ideas of the Modem School* (London, 1913)

title: Attempted assassination of Alfonso XIII
summary: Jose Sancho Alegre, a young Anarchist from Barcelona, tried to kill Alfonso XIII at a military parade in Madrid. The attempt failed and Sancho Alegre was condemned to death, then commuted.

citation.quote: In April of the following year, another young Anarchist from Barcelona, Jose Sancho Alegre, tried to kill Alfonso XIII at a military parade in Madrid.

title: Death of Anselmo Lorenzo
summary: The grand patriarch of Spanish Anarchism, Anselmo Lorenzo, died on November 30, 1914, having devoted almost a half century to the libertarian movement.

citation.quote: In any case this grand patriarch of Spanish Anarchism died on November 30, 1914, having devoted almost a half century to the libertarian movement.

title: Banned antiwar congress in Ferrol
summary: The Ateneo Sindicalista of Ferrol tried to hold an international antiwar congress attracting delegates from Portugal, Brazil and other countries. Conservative premier Eduardo Dato banned the meeting.

citation.quote: In the spring of 1915, the Ateneo Sindicalista of Ferrol tried to hold an international antiwar congress, an event which attracted delegates from Portugal, Brazil, and other countries, including representatives of Socialist youth groups in France.

title: Solidaridad Obrera becomes a daily newspaper
summary: By 1916, the CNT had recovered sufficiently to publish Solidaridad Obrera as a daily newspaper, though the movement was still subjected to severe harassment.

citation.quote: By 1916 the labor organization had recovered sufficiently to publish Solidaridad Obrera as a daily newspaper, but the movement was still subjected to severe harassment.

title: Anarchist action group offers atentado services to CNT
summary: Two young anarchist workers approached Angel Pestana, then editor of Solidaridad Obrera, offering to carry out atentados against employers on behalf of the organization in exchange for expenses and a reserve fund.

citation.quote: In 1916 Angel Pestana, who at that time was editor of Solidaridad Obrera, was privately approached by two young workers who, without any preliminaries, declared:

title: CNT-UGT joint 24-hour general strike
summary: Under the 'Pact of Saragossa,' the CNT and the UGT carried off an impressive twenty-four-hour general strike throughout Spain to protest rising prices.

citation.quote: The movement reached its culmination when on December 16, 1916, the two labor organizations carried off an impressive twenty-four-hour general strike throughout Spain to protest rising prices.

title: Andalusian Anarchist Federation established
summary: An Andalusian Anarchist Federation was established, part of the trend of Anarchist groups forming into regional federations that later combined into the National Federation of Anarchist Groups and eventually the FAI.

citation.quote: An Andalusian Anarchist Federation had been established in 1917, and now there was one in Catalonia as well as other provinces.

title: Dato dissolves the Cortes and suspends constitutional guarantees
summary: Newly appointed premier Dato responded to mounting revolutionary threat by dissolving the Cortes and suspending constitutional guarantees. Catalan deputies declared themselves a National Assembly.

citation.quote: In June, Dato, the newly appointed premier, responded to the mounting revolutionary threat by dissolving the Cortes and suspending constitutional guarantees.

title: Durruti shifts allegiance to the CNT
summary: At the time of the August 1917 general strike, the young Durruti shifted his allegiance from the UGT to the militant Anarchosyndicalist CNT.

citation.quote: at the time of the August 1917 general strike he shifted his allegiance to the Anarchosyndicalist union.

title: General strike of August 1917
summary: The general strike was called on August 13, smashed within days. Heavy fighting in Barcelona left officially seventy killed, hundreds wounded, and some two thousand arrested. Socialist leaders received life sentences.

citation.quote: The general strike was called on August 13, and in most areas it was smashed within a few days. Heavy fighting had broken out in a number of cities, particularly in Barcelona, where the CNT reluctantly honored its agreement with its Socialist allies.

title: Trieno Bolchevista (Bolshevik Triennium) in Andalusia
summary: With general strikes in the north and the success of the Russian Revolution, an intoxicating wave of hope swept through the south initiating the Bolshevik Triennium of 1918–20, when Anarchist propaganda inundated the countryside.

citation.quote: With the outbreak of general strikes in the north and the success of the Russian Revolution, an intoxicating wave of hope swept through the south initiating the Trieno Bolchevista or "Bolshevik Triennium" of 1918–20.

title: CNT launches massive propaganda campaign across Spain
summary: During the summer of 1918, the CNT launched a massive propaganda campaign throughout most of Spain, increasing its Catalan membership nearly fivefold from 75,000 in June to 350,000 by year's end.

citation.quote: During the summer of 1918, the CNT launched a massive propaganda campaign throughout most of Spain to win over the working class. Within six months, the labor organization had increased its Catalan membership nearly fivefold, leaping from 75,000 in June to 350,000 by the end of the year.

title: Andalusian Regional Confederation founded at Seville congress
summary: A congress at Seville established the Anarchist Andalusian regional confederation and first adopted the sindicatos unicos for a Spanish syndicalist union, paving the way for their acceptance in Catalonia and the CNT.

citation.quote: But the Catalan gathering had been inspired in great measure by Anarchist Andalusia, where a regional confederation had been established on May 1st in a congress at Seville. It was at this Seville congress, in fact, that the sindicates unicos were adopted for the first time by a Spanish syndicalist union...

title: Pestana exposes Bravo Portillo's German espionage ring
summary: Angel Pestana published evidence in Solidaridad Obrera that district police chief Manuel Bravo Portillo was operating a German espionage ring in the port area of Barcelona.

citation.quote: Perhaps the most sensational example of these sinister connections was revealed in the pages of Solidaridad Obrera on June 8, 1918, when Pestana published evidence that a district police chief, Manuel Bravo Portillo, was operating a German espionage ring in the port area.

title: Congress of Sans of the Catalan Regional Confederation
summary: A four-day assembly of 164 delegates representing 73,860 members in twenty-seven local federations convened in Barcelona, restructuring syndicates into industrial sindicatos unicos.

citation.quote: Buenacasa's conclusion, however, should not be too hastily accepted, as witness the results of the congress of the Catalan Regional Confederation (the famous "congress of Sans") convened in Barcelona on June 28,1918. This four-day assembly was attended by 164 delegates, representing some 73,860 members in twenty-seven local federations.

title: National Anarchist conference in Barcelona on CNT policy
summary: Anarchists from across Spain met in Barcelona to define a common policy toward the CNT, agreeing the union should be a major arena of Anarchist activity and urging members to enter and proselytize it.

citation.quote: In the winter of 1918 a national Anarchist conference was held in Barcelona to define a common policy toward the CNT.

title: CNT wins over Federation National de Agricultores at Valencia
summary: While stopping at Valencia, Buenacasa and his comrades won over to the CNT the entire Federation National de Agricultores during its fifth national congress, along with the Regional Workers' Federation of Andalusia.

citation.quote: In some cases, the gains were utterly spectacular: in December, for example, while stopping at Valencia, Buenacasa and his comrades won over to the CNT the entire Federation National de Agricultores, which was then holding its fifth national congress.

title: CNT reaches 600,000 to one million members
summary: By 1919, the CNT had grown to between 600,000 and a million members, absorbing most older established unions in Catalonia after surviving wartime government attacks.

citation.quote: The labor organization had emerged from the war years and the general strike stronger than ever: by 1919, the CNT numbered from 600,000 to a million members.

title: FNA dissolves into the CNT
summary: The Federation National de Agricultores held regular annual congresses up to 1919, when it dissolved into the CNT.

citation.quote: Generally, the success of this new organization had been modest although it succeeded in holding regular annual congresses up to 1919, when it dissolved into the CNT.

title: Romanones suspends constitutional guarantees in Catalonia
summary: Romanones decreed the suspension of all constitutional guarantees in Catalonia; top CNT officials including Buenacasa, Segui, Herreros, and Negre were rounded up and imprisoned on the battleship Pelayo at Barcelona.

citation.quote: Finally, on January 16, 1919, Romanones decreed the suspension of all constitutional guarantees in Catalonia. Nearly all the top CNT officials, including Buenacasa, Segui, Herreros, and Negre, were rounded up and imprisoned in the battleship "Pelayo" lying at anchor in Barcelona.

title: Canadiense clerical staff begins sit-in strike
summary: After eight clerks were discharged, the entire clerical staff of the Anglo-Canadian hydroelectric company declared a sit-in strike, triggering the legendary Canadiense general strike in Barcelona.

citation.quote: Three days later, on February 5, the entire clerical staff declared a sit-in strike and sent a committee to the highest public officials of Catalonia requesting their intervention in the conflict.

title: Canadiense strike spreads as Energia Electrica workers sit-in
summary: Workers of the Energia Electrica de Cataluna struck in solidarity with the Canadiense, sitting-in in their own plant and beginning the strike's spread to strategic sectors.

citation.quote: On the same day that the "Canadiense" went on strike (February 8), the workers of the Energia Electrica de Cataluna followed them in an act of solidarity, sitting-in in their own plant.

title: Barcelona textile workers walk out
summary: Nine days into the Canadiense strike, the textile workers walked out, followed by a near-complete strike of all electrical workers, plunging Barcelona into darkness.

citation.quote: Nine days later, on February 17, the textile workers walked out. They were followed by a nearly complete strike by all the electrical workers of Barcelona. The city was plunged into darkness.

title: Romanones decrees eight-hour day in Spain
summary: Romanones decreed an eight-hour day for the construction workers, to be extended to all trades on April 3, making Spain the first country in the world to enact the eight-hour day into law.

citation.quote: Finally, on March 11, Romanones had tried to curry favor with the strikers by decreeing an eight-hour day for the construction workers, which was to be extended to all trades on April 3. The decree made Spain the first country in the world to enact the eight-hour day into law.

title: Romanones installs Montanes and Doval in Barcelona
summary: By March 13, Romanones installed Carlos Montanes as civil governor and Gerardo Doval as Barcelona police chief, both well-known for their liberal views, pursuing a policy of negotiation with the strikers.

citation.quote: By March 13, the frantic Romanones, pursuing a policy of negotiation with the strikers, installed Carlos Montanes as civil governor and Gerardo Doval as Barcelona police chief—both well-known for their liberal views.

title: Canadiense settlement approved at Las Arenas mass meeting
summary: On the night of March 16, the strike settlement was submitted to a huge mass meeting at Barcelona's plaza de toros de Las Arenas; workers agreed to return to work but threatened to resume the strike if prisoners were not freed in 72 hours.

citation.quote: On the night of March 16, the settlement was submitted for approval to a huge mass meeting of strikers at Barcelona's plaza de toros de Las Arenas.

title: Canadiense strike resumes after prisoner release deadline missed
summary: When the government let the seventy-two hours pass without releasing the remaining prisoners, the strike was resumed in full force on March 24, prompting Milans del Bosch to act with energy and decisiveness.

citation.quote: Despite pleas by union officials, the government let the seventy-two hours pass without releasing the remaining prisoners. There was no way to avoid this challenge, and on March 24, wisely or not, the strike was resumed in full force.

title: Canadiense general strike ends
summary: By April 7, the general strike had essentially come to an end as metallurgical workers, the last to hold out, returned to work; Milans del Bosch's repression broke the strike and toppled the Romanones government.

citation.quote: The metallurgical workers held out to the last, but by April 7 the general strike had essentially come to an end.

title: General La Berrera sent into Andalusia with troops
summary: The new Maura ministry sent General La Berrera into the south with a division of troops; martial law was declared, workers' centers closed, radical newspapers suppressed, and thousands arrested.

citation.quote: Finally, in May 1919, the new Maura ministry sent General La Berrera into the south with a division of troops. The soldiers, divided into small detachments, occupied virtually all the restive towns and villages.

title: Assassination of Pablo Sabater
summary: Two men in police uniforms drove up to the home of Pablo Sabater, president of the Barcelona textile union, and shot him to death, intensifying pistolerismo in the city.

citation.quote: On the night of July 19, two men in police uniforms drove up to the home of Pablo Sabater, the president of the textile union, and shot him to death.

title: Agreement reached for return of 70,000 Barcelona workers
summary: Under Sanchez de Toca's conciliatory ministry and civil governor Julio Amado's Mixed Commission of Labor, an agreement was reached for the return of 70,000 workers (many of them lockouts as well as strikers) to their jobs.

citation.quote: For a while, it almost seemed that Amado's policy of conciliation might succeed: the number of atentados fell off sharply, and an agreement was reached in September for the return of 70,000 workers (many of them lockouts as well as strikers) to their jobs.

title: Assassination of Manuel Bravo Portillo
summary: Former police captain Manuel Bravo Portillo, who had been running a pistolero gang for the employers, was shot down at noon in the Calle de Santa Tecla in Barcelona.

citation.quote: Bravo, in turn, did not survive the summer. On September 15, at noon, he was shot down in the Calle de Santa Tecla.

title: Killing of Eduardo Ferrer
summary: Two days after Bravo Portillo's assassination, Eduardo Ferrer, a former leader in the metallurgical union and one of Bravo's most detested agents, was killed.

citation.quote: Two days afterward, one of his most detested agents, Eduardo Ferrer, a former leader in the metallurgical union, was killed.

title: Employers' Federations secretly vote for general lockout
summary: A congress of the Employers' Federations in Barcelona secretly voted to initiate a general lockout in Catalonia and, if necessary, throughout Spain.

citation.quote: In October 1919, a congress of the Employers' Federations in Barcelona secretly voted to initiate a general lockout in Catalonia and, if necessary, throughout Spain, in the event that the government should fail to end the "present situation of social disorganization."

title: Catalan general lockout begins
summary: When 25,000 construction workers went on strike, the employers initiated their lockout the same day, throwing 200,000 out of work; the action lasted ten bitter weeks into January 1920.

citation.quote: When, on November 25, some 25,000 construction workers went on strike, the employers apparently decided that-the opportune moment for their offensive had arrived. The lockout began on the very same day, throwing 200,000 out of work.

title: CNT launches campaign to sweep Andalusia
summary: By December 1919, a major campaign had been launched to sweep Andalusia into the CNT, with local newspapers, speakers, pamphlets, and leaflets flowing through the south.

citation.quote: By December 1919, a major campaign had been launched to sweep Andalusia into the CNT. Local newspapers were started up in dozens of towns, and a stream of Anarchist speakers, pamphlets, and leaflets flowed through the south.

title: Founding of the sindicato libre
summary: Carlist Ramon Sales founded the sindicato libre (free union) at the Ateneo Legitimista in Barcelona, patronized by the church and employers and used to divide the labor movement.

citation.quote: In December 1919, the Carlist Ramon Sales founded the sindicato libre (free union) at the Ateneo, Legitimista in Barcelona.

title: Second National Congress of the CNT opens in Madrid
summary: 437 delegates representing over 700,000 members gathered in the Teatro de la Comedia for the CNT's second national congress, which declared its belief in comunismo anarquico and adopted the sindicato unico.

citation.quote: On the morning of December 10,1919,437 delegates gathered in the aristocratic Teatro de la Comedia, filling most of the orchestra seats and boxes.

title: Murder of Francisco Layret
summary: Republican deputy and CNT lawyer Francisco Layret was murdered shortly after his colleague Luis Companys was arrested.

citation.quote: the lawyer Luis Companys was arrested and shortly afterward his colleague, the popular Republican deputy Francisco Layret, was murdered.

title: Assassination of the Conde de Salvatierra
summary: The Conde de Salvatierra, civil governor of Catalonia who had presided over the lockout of late 1919 and early 1920, fell before the guns of Anarchist pistoleros.

citation.quote: In 1920, the civil governor of Catalonia, the Conde de Salvatierra, who had presided over the lockout of late 1919 and early 1920, fell before the guns of Anarchist pistoleros.

title: Attempt on Salvador Segui's life
summary: An assassination attempt was made on CNT leader Salvador Segui, prompting Anarchist reprisal atentados against the president of the Employers' Federation, one of its directors, and two police agents.

citation.quote: Following an attempt on Segui's life on January 4, 1920, the Anarchists responded with atentados against the president of the Employers' Federation, one of its directors, and two police agents.

title: Baron Koenig expelled from Spain
summary: Foreign adventurer 'Baron Koenig,' who had taken over Bravo Portillo's gang and extorted protection money from employers, was quietly expelled from Spain and his gang dissolved.

citation.quote: Accordingly, in the late spring of 1920, he was quietly expelled from Spain and his gang dissolved.

title: Pestana sent to Moscow to represent CNT at Comintern Second Congress
summary: Angel Pestana was sent to Moscow to represent the CNT at the Second Congress of the Communist International, where he was courted by Zinoviev and Losovsky but sensed the gap between libertarian ideals and Bolshevik practices.

citation.quote: In June 1920, Angel Pestana was sent to Moscow to represent the labor organization at the Second Congress of the Communist International.

title: Rio Tinto miners' strike begins
summary: The CNT-led strike of the Rio Tinto copper miners in Andalusia began, becoming one of the most bitter disputes in the history of the Spanish labor movement.

citation.quote: The strike, which began in June 1920, was led by the CNT.

title: CNT-UGT pact signed in Madrid
summary: CNT moderates Segui, Boal, and Quemades signed a defensive pact with UGT leaders including Largo Caballero in Madrid, demanding restoration of constitutional guarantees.

citation.quote: On September 3, 1920, these moderates signed a pact which advanced a demand for the restoration of constitutional guarantees.

title: Bomb at Paralelo dance hall
summary: A bomb exploded in a working-class dance hall on the Paralelo in Barcelona, killing three and wounding twenty in one of the most senseless atrocities of the pistol war.

citation.quote: One of the most senseless atrocities occurred on the night of September 12, when a bomb exploded in a working-class dance hall on the Paralelo, killing three and wounding twenty.

title: Assassination of E. Tarrida
summary: E. Tarrida, head of a metallurgical firm, was assassinated about a month after the Paralelo dance hall bombing.

citation.quote: A month later, the head of a metallurgical firm, E. Tarrida, was assassinated.

title: Martinez Anido appointed civil governor of Catalonia
summary: Captain general Severino Martinez Anido was appointed civil governor of Catalonia, replacing Carlos Bas, an act denounced as defiance of moderate and humane opinion.

citation.quote: To worsen a rapidly deteriorating situation, in November 1920 the captain general of Catalonia, Severino Martinez Anido, was appointed civil governor, replacing Carlos Bas.

title: Assassination of Jaime Pujal
summary: Jaime Pujal, president of the Association of Electrical Employers, was killed two weeks after the murder of E. Tarrida.

citation.quote: This was followed two weeks later by the death of Jaime Pujal, president of the Association of Electrical Employers.

title: Arrest of sixty-four CNT officials
summary: The arrest of sixty-four CNT officials in Barcelona led to a general protest strike.

citation.quote: The arrest of sixty-four CNT officials on November 20 led to a general protest strike.

title: Martinez Anido outlaws the CNT
summary: Civil governor Martinez Anido responded to the general protest strike by outlawing the CNT labor federation and reestablishing censorship.

citation.quote: On November 23, Martinez Anido responded by outlawing the labor federation and reestablishing censorship.

title: Killing of sindicato libre president of Reus
summary: Three days after Martinez Anido outlawed the CNT, the president of the sindicato libre of Reus was killed.

citation.quote: Three days later, the president of the sindicato libre of Reus was killed.

title: Assassination of Jose Canela
summary: Jose Canela, an important member of the Regional Committee of the CNT, was assassinated the day after the killing of the sindicato libre president of Reus.

citation.quote: His death was followed the very next day by the assassination of Jose Canela, an important member of the Regional Committee of the CNT.

title: Sastre y Sama's La Esclavitud Moderna published
summary: Miguel Sastre y Sama's La Esclavitud Moderna was published in Barcelona, addressing the pistolerismo period.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: Miguel Sastre y Sama's *La Esclavitud Modema* (Barcelona, 1921).

title: Soviet regime suppresses Kronstadt sailors uprising
summary: The Soviet regime harshly suppressed the Kronstadt sailors uprising; coupled with a mounting campaign against Russian Anarchists, this began to alienate the libertarian movement worldwide from the Bolsheviks.

citation.quote: In March 1921, the Soviet regime harshly suppressed the Kronstadt sailors uprising. The Kronstadt issue, coupled with a mounting campaign against Russian Anarchists, began to alienate the libertarian movement throughout the world.

title: Assassination of Premier Eduardo Dato
summary: Conservative premier Eduardo Dato was killed by three Catalan Anarchists in reprisal for restoring the Ley de fugas, the practice in which police killed arrested syndicalists claiming they were shot trying to escape.

citation.quote: On March 8, 1921, the Conservative premier, Eduardo Dato, was killed by three Catalan Anarchists in reprisal for restoring the Ley de fugas (Law of Flight)

title: Nin and Maurin surface in Moscow claiming CNT representation
summary: Andres Nin and Joaquin Maurin appeared in Moscow professing to represent the CNT and, without consulting the movement, affiliated it to the Communist International; their actions were later disavowed at the Logrono plenum.

citation.quote: In April 1921, a group headed by Andres Nin and Joaquin Maurin surfaced in Moscow, professing to represent the CNT.

title: Disaster at Annual in Spanish Morocco
summary: A large Spanish column under General Silvestre advancing from Melilla to Alhucemas was ambushed at Annual by Riff tribesmen and virtually destroyed, with ten thousand killed and four thousand captured.

citation.quote: Two years earlier, in June 1921, a large column in Spanish Morocco, advancing under the command of General Silvestre from Melilla to Alhucemas, was ambushed at Annual and virtually destroyed by a smaller force of Riff tribesmen.

title: Killing of Evelio Baal
summary: Evelio Baal, general secretary of the CNT National Committee, was killed at dawn minutes after being released by the police.

citation.quote: the CNT paid a corresponding price with the death of Evelio Baal, the general secretary of the National Committee, killed at dawn on June 15, minutes after having been released by the police.

title: CNT plenum at Logrono disavows Nin and Maurin
summary: A plenum of the CNT at Logrono disavowed the actions and claims of Nin and Maurin, who had affiliated the union to the Communist International without authorization.

citation.quote: Their actions and claims were disavowed by a plenum of the CNT at Logrono the following August.

title: Dismissal of Martinez Anido
summary: After ruling Barcelona for two years and shocking public opinion across Spain, Martinez Anido was finally dismissed as civil governor, prompted in part by the scandal over orders to shoot Pestana outside a hospital.

citation.quote: After ruling Barcelona for two years in a manner that had completely shocked public opinion throughout Spain, this brutal soldier was finally dismissed in 1922.

title: Farre Morego's Los Atentados Sociales en Espana published
summary: Maria Farre Morego's Los Atentados Sociales en Espana was published in Madrid, dealing with the pistolerismo phase of Spanish Anarchosyndicalism.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: The reader who is interested in this phase of Spanish Anarchosyndicalism may care to consult Maria Farre Morego's Los Atentados *Sociales en Espana* (Madrid, 1922)

title: Durruti arrives in Barcelona; 'Solidarios' takes form
summary: With Durruti's arrival in Barcelona in January 1922, the 'Solidarios' action group began to take form. Obliged to use an alias, Durruti operated in the underground.

citation.quote: With Durruti's arrival in Barcelona in January 1922, the Solidarios began to take form as an action group.

title: Constitutional guarantees restored in Spain
summary: In April 1922, constitutional guarantees were restored in Spain for the first time in nearly a year and a half, lifting the atmosphere of repression and isolation.

citation.quote: In April 1922, constitutional guarantees were restored for the first time in nearly a year and a half.

title: CNT Saragossa conference rejects Bolshevik affiliation
summary: A conference of the CNT at Saragossa rejected affiliation with the Bolshevik movement, and the CNT with other independent syndicalist unions began exploring a new international.

citation.quote: On June 11, 1922, a conference of the CNT at Saragossa rejected affiliation with the Bolshevik movement, and the CNT together with other independent syndicalist unions in Europe, began to explore the possibility of forming a new international.

title: CNT national conference in Saragossa
summary: The CNT held a successful national conference in Saragossa where forty-two delegates broke all ties with the Communist International and passed resolutions favored by the moderates.

citation.quote: The CNT, reemerging from a harassed clandestinity, managed to hold a successful national conference on June 11 in Saragossa. The forty-two delegates who attended the conference broke all ties with the Communist International.

title: Syndicalist International Workingmen's Association founded in Berlin
summary: The syndicalist international, bearing the traditional name of International Workingmen's Association, was founded at a congress held in Berlin; the CNT's adherence ruptured all ties with Moscow.

citation.quote: Bearing the traditional name of "International Workingmen's Association," the syndicalist international was founded at a congress held in Berlin from December 26, 1922, to January 3, 1923.

title: Assassination of Salvador Segui
summary: Salvador Segui and his companion Francisco Comas were shot down in Barcelona's Calle de la Cadena during the busiest part of the day, removing the most influential moderate spokesman in the CNT.

citation.quote: As if to symbolize the end of the postwar era, on March 10, 1923, Salvador Segui and a companion, Francisco Comas, were shot down in Barcelona's Calle de la Cadena.

title: 'Solidarios' track Martinez Anido
summary: Members of the 'Solidarios,' armed with sub-machine guns and bombs, tracked Martinez Anido to San Sebastian and then pursued him to La Coruna, but he disappeared underground.

citation.quote: In May 1923, the Solidarios, armed with sub-machine guns and bombs, tracked him to San Sebastian, but he had fled to La Coruna, where they pursued him again.

title: Assassination of Fernando Gonzalez Regueral
summary: Anarchist pistoleros of the 'Solidarios' group from Barcelona assassinated Fernando Gonzalez Regueral, the former governor of Vizcaya, in reprisal for Segui's murder.

citation.quote: On May 17, 1923, Anarchist pistoleros from Barcelona assassinated Fernando Gonzalez Regueral, the former governor of Vizcaya.

title: Assassination of Cardinal Soldevila y Romero
summary: Members of the 'Solidarios' Anarchist action group killed Cardinal Juan Soldevila y Romero, the Archbishop of Saragossa, three weeks after the Regueral assassination.

citation.quote: Three weeks later, on June 11, they killed Cardinal Juan Soldevila y Romero, the Archbishop of Saragossa.

title: 'Solidarios' rob the Bank of Gijon
summary: A group of 'Solidarios' held up the Bank of Gijon, making off with over 600,000 pesetas in one of the largest expropriations of its day.

citation.quote: the most famous of which occurred on September 1, 1923, when a group of Solidarios held up the Bank of Gijon, making off with over 600,000 pesetas.

title: Primo de Rivera proclaims himself military dictator of Spain
summary: General Miguel Primo de Rivera, captain general of Catalonia, declared himself military dictator of Spain, ending the parliamentary oligarchy created by Sagasta.

citation.quote: On September 13, 1923, General Miguel Primo de Rivera, the ^captain general of Catalonia (a post to which he had been appointed during the previous year), proclaimed himself military dictator of Spain, bringing to an end the parliamentary oligarchy Sagasta had labored to create in the 1870s.

title: CNT declares general strike against Primo's dictatorship
summary: A day after Primo's pronunciamiento, the CNT declared a general strike, which was easily suppressed by the military due to lack of Socialist support and inadequate preparation.

citation.quote: On September 14, a day after Primo's *pronunciamiento*, the CNT declared a general strike. In the absence of Socialist support and sufficient time for adequate preparation, the strike was easily suppressed by the military.

title: 'Solidarios' purchase 1,000 rifles in Eibar
summary: As the day of the planned uprising against Primo de Rivera's dictatorship approached, the Solidarios group bought 1,000 rifles and 200,000 cartridges from the firm of Garate y Anitua in Eibar. The insurrection never came off.

citation.quote: In October 1923, as the day of the uprising approached, the group managed to buy 1,000 rifles and 200,000 cartridges from the firm of Garate y Anitua in the town of Eibar.

title: Durruti flees Spain for France
summary: By December 1923, Durruti's position had become so precarious that he was forced to leave Spain and take refuge in France.

citation.quote: By December 1923 Durruti's position had become so precarious that it was necessary for him to leave Spain and take refuge in France.

title: Catalan Regional Confederation plenum at Granollers
summary: The Catalan Regional Confederation of the CNT held a plenum at Granollers attended by hundreds of workers, reaffirming the union's commitment to Anarchist principles.

citation.quote: On December 30, 1923, the Catalan Regional Confederation held a plenum at Granollers which attracted hundreds of workers; this was followed on May 4, 1924, by another plenum at Sabadell.

title: Plot to kidnap King Alfonso in Paris
summary: Durruti, Ascaso, and Grigorio Jover plotted to kidnap King Alfonso during his state visit to Paris in order to demand the dissolution of the dictatorship; they were arrested by French police.

citation.quote: Perhaps the most renowned of the Anarchist conspiracies during the dictatorship was an audacious plot hatched by Durruti, Ascaso, and Grigorio Jover to kidnap the king during a state visit to Paris in the summer of 1924.

title: Murder of Suberbiela and Campos
summary: According to Sanz, the secret police murdered Gregorio Suberbiela and Manuel Campos, two members of the 'Solidarios,' marking the dissolution of the group as the Primo de Rivera dictatorship consolidated.

citation.quote: In February 1924, the secret police (according to Sanz) had murdered Gregorio Suberbiela and Manuel Campos, two members of the Solidarios.

title: Municipal Statute proposed by Primo's regime
summary: The Municipal Statute promised extensive autonomy to municipalities but was stillborn, leaving towns in the hands of government appointees.

citation.quote: Proposed structural reforms, such as the Municipal Statute of March 1924, which promised to give extensive autonomy to the municipalities, were stillborn, leaving the restive towns in the hands of government appointees.

title: CNT Catalan Regional plenum at Sabadell
summary: The CNT's Catalan Regional Confederation held another plenum at Sabadell, again reaffirming its commitment to Anarchist principles.

citation.quote: On December 30, 1923, the Catalan Regional Confederation held a plenum at Granollers which attracted hundreds of workers; this was followed on May 4, 1924, by another plenum at Sabadell.

title: Assassination of Barcelona police official and CNT crackdown
summary: Three days after the Sabadell plenum, Anarchist terrorists assassinated Barcelona police official Rogelio Perez Cicario, after which the government cracked down on the CNT, arresting committee members and Anarchists.

citation.quote: Three days after the Sabadell plenum. Anarchist terrorists assassinated an onerous Barcelona police official, one Rogelio Perez Cicario ("el ejecutor de la justicia"), whereupon' the government immediately cracked down on the syndicalist labor union, rounding up all the CNT committee members and members of Anarchist groups it could find.

title: Anarchist attacks on Atarazanas barracks and Vera de Bidasoa
summary: Small groups of Anarchist militants attacked the Atarazanas barracks in Barcelona while exiles led by Durruti crossed from France to invade Vera de Bidasoa. Both attempts failed; captured participants were executed.

citation.quote: On November 6, 1924, small groups of militants attacked the Atarazanas barracks in Barcelona, apparently assured that the fortress gates would be opened by supporters within. At the same time, a small armed band of Anarchist exiles in France, led by Durruti, crossed the frontier and invaded Vera de Bidasoa, clashing with the Civil Guard.

title: Nettlau publishes Miguel Bakunin, la Internacional y la Alianza en España
summary: Max Nettlau's research on Bakunin, the International, and the Alliance in Spain was originally published in Buenos Aires.

citation.quote: Max Nettlau's *Miguel Bakunin, la International y la Alianza en Espana* (originally published in Buenos Aires, 1925)

title: Primo lifts martial law
summary: Primo de Rivera lifted the state of martial law, allowing social life in Spain to ease and Anarchist and syndicalist periodicals to begin reappearing.

citation.quote: In May 1925, Primo lifted the state of martial law, and social life in Spain began to ease considerably.

title: Mella's Ideario published in Gijon
summary: Ricardo Mella's Ideario is published in Gijon, constituting Volume One of the Obras Completas de Ricardo Mella.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Ricardo Mella's *Ideario* (Gijon, 1926) and *Ensayos y Conferencias* (Gijon, 1934), both of which constitute Volumes One and Two respectively

title: "Night of St. John" conspiracy
summary: The moderate-dominated National Committee of the CNT became involved in an abortive conspiracy known as the "Night of St. John," possibly conceived by the monarchy to unseat Primo and restore constitutional government.

citation.quote: Two years later, in June 1926, it had become involved in an abortive conspiracy known as the "Night of St. John," a plot which may have been conceived by the monarchy itself in order to rescue its waning reputation by unseating Primo and reestablishing a constitutional government.

title: Communist Party seizes Seville dock CNT syndicates
summary: The Spanish Communist Party won control over a number of underground CNT syndicates in Seville, principally in the dock area, providing a base for duels with rival Anarchosyndicalist and Socialist unions.

citation.quote: in 1927 it had managed to win control over a considerable number of underground CNT syndicates in Seville—principally in the dock area— which it began to use as a base for duels with rival Anarchosyndicalist and Socialist unions.

title: Founding conference of the FAI at Valencia
summary: A clandestine conference of Spanish and Portuguese Anarchists was held at Valencia, timed to coincide with a fiesta, giving birth to the Federacion Anarquista Iberica (FAI).

citation.quote: On July 24 and 25, 1927, a clandestine conference of Spanish and Portuguese Anarchists was held at Valencia.

title: Widespread student protests against the dictatorship
summary: Widespread student protests presented the Primo dictatorship with its first overt opposition since 1924.

citation.quote: In the spring of 1928, widespread student protests presented the dictatorship with its first overt opposition since 1924.

title: Kropotkin's Revolutionary Pamphlets published in New York
summary: Peter Kropotkin's Revolutionary Pamphlets, containing his essay 'Anarchist Communism: Its Basis and Principles,' is published in New York.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Peter Kropotkin's early essay "Anarchist Communism: Its Basis and Principles" (*Revolutionary Pamphlets* \[New York, 1928\])

title: CNT clandestine plenum in Barcelona authorizes negotiations
summary: The CNT's National Committee convoked a clandestine plenum in Barcelona to authorize negotiations with antidictatorial politicians and military leaders.

citation.quote: On July 28, 1928, the National Committee convoked a clandestine plenum in Barcelona, including delegates from all the regions except for the volatile Levant, with the purpose o. authorizing negotiations with antidictatorial politicians and military leaders.

title: Nettlau's articles on Spanish socialism appear in La Revista Blanca
summary: Max Nettlau's series of articles 'Impresiones historicas sobre el desarrollo del Socialismo en Espana' were published in La Revista Blanca.

citation.quote: his highly informative articles in *La Reuista Blanca* (September 1, 1928 — May 1,1929), published under the title, "Impresiones historicas sobre el desarrollo del Socialismo en Espana,"

title: Díaz del Moral publishes Historia de las Agitaciones Campesinas Andaluzas
summary: Juan Diaz del Moral's classic history of Andalusian peasant agitations was originally published in Madrid.

citation.quote: Juan Diaz del Moral's *Historia de las Agitaciones Campesinas Andaluzas* (originally published in Madrid, 1929)

title: Nettlau publishes essay on Spanish Socialism in La Revista Blanca
summary: Nettlau's 'Impresiones historicas sobre el desarrollo del Socialismo en España' is published in La Revista Blanca (Numero 140, 1929).

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Nettlau's "Impresiones historicas sobre el desarrollo del Socialismo en Espana" in *La Revista Blanca* (Numero 140, 1929) is informative

title: Primo polls captain generals on army support
summary: Primo de Rivera circulated a query to the captain generals asking if the army supported him, threatening to resign if it did not.

citation.quote: On January 26, Primo, agonized by growing internal opposition and fiscal difficulties, .circulated a query to the captain generals, asking if the army supported him.

title: Primo de Rivera resigns
summary: Primo de Rivera resigned and departed for Paris, where he died a few months later. General Damaso Berenguer took his place.

citation.quote: On January 28, 1929, two days after his query, Primo de Rivera resigned and departed for the fleshpots of Paris, where he died a few months later.

title: FAI issues first public manifesto
summary: The FAI's Peninsular Committee issued its first public statement, a manifesto sharply denouncing the moderate tendency in the CNT.

citation.quote: In December of that year, the Peninsular Committee issued its first public statement as an organization—a manifesto that sharply denounced the moderate tendency in the CNT.

title: UGT membership before Primo's fall
summary: Shortly before Primo de Rivera's fall, the UGT could claim 1,511 local sections with about 230,000 members.

citation.quote: In December 1929, shortly before Primo's fall, it could claim 1,511 local sections with about 230,000 members.

title: Communist conference on Syndicalist Reconstruction
summary: The Spanish Communist Party convened a conference on Syndicalist Reconstruction, giving rise to the Stalinist-manipulated 'Committee of Reconstruction' that contested Seville unions with the CNT and UGT.

citation.quote: the Stalinist-manipulated "Committee of Reconstruction," so named because of a conference on Syndicalist Reconstruction which the party had convened in the spring of 1930.

title: Nettlau publishes Documentos Inéditos sobre la Internacional y la Alianza en España
summary: Max Nettlau's collection of unpublished documents on the International and the Alliance in Spain was published in Buenos Aires.

citation.quote: notably Nettlau's *Documentos Ineditos sobre la International y la Alianza en Espana* (Buenos Aires, 1930)

title: Morato publishes Historia de la Sección Española de la Internacional
summary: Juan Jose Morato's history of the Spanish section of the International (1868–1874) was published in Madrid.

citation.quote: Juan Jose Morato's *Historia de la Section Espanola de la International, 1868–1874* (Madrid, 1930)

title: Berenguer replaces Primo
summary: The replacement of Primo by Berenguer in January 1930 completely altered the de facto status of the CNT, allowing many syndicates to function openly.

citation.quote: The replacement of Primo by Berenguer in January 1930 completely altered the *de facto* status of the CNT and many syndicates began to function openly even before they acquired official legality.

title: UGT founds rural federation FNTT
summary: The UGT established a separate rural federation, the FNTT (Federation National de Trabajadores de la Tierra), beginning with a membership of only 27,000.

citation.quote: In April 1930, the UGT established a separate rural federation, the FNTT or Federation National de Trabajadores de la Tierra (National Federation of Land Workers). It began with a membership of only 27,000

title: CNT granted conditional legality in Barcelona
summary: The CNT was granted a form of "conditional" legality by the governor of Barcelona, followed by legalization in other provinces.

citation.quote: On April 30, 1930, the CNT was granted a form of "conditional" legality by the governor of Barcelona, followed by legalization in other provinces.

title: First plenum of CNT Catalan Regional Federation
summary: The first plenum of the Catalan Regional Federation initiated a drive to publish Solidaridad Obrera as a daily newspaper.

citation.quote: The first plenum of the Catalan Regional Federation, held on May 17, 1930, initiated a drive to publish *Solidaridad Obrera* as a daily.

title: Pact of San Sebastian signed
summary: Republican factions resolved conflicts over Catalan autonomy by signing the Pact of San Sebastian, promising far-reaching autonomy to Catalonia and pledging revolutionary action against the monarchy.

citation.quote: The gnawing conflicts over Catalan autonomy, which divided Republican ranks between Catalans and Spaniards, were resolved in August 1930, when both wings signed the famous Pact of San Sebastian.

title: Solidaridad Obrera legalized in Barcelona
summary: Solidaridad Obrera in Barcelona began appearing as a daily shortly after it was legalized on August 30, 1930.

citation.quote: *Solidaridad Obrera* in Barcelona began to appear as a daily shortly after it was legalized on August 30 and, following the custom of the predictatorial years, sister publications with the same name began to spring up in other cities of Spain.

title: Barcelona general strike
summary: The CNT staged a successful general strike in Barcelona running from November 17 through November 24, spreading to other townships and filling the jails so full that anchored ships were used to supplement them.

citation.quote: The end of the strike was fixed for November 20 (it had started on the 17th) but the workers had continued it to the 24th. It had spread to various important townships in the region and the jails were so full that a number of ships anchored in the harbor had to be used to supplement them.

title: Jaca rebellion and failed Republican uprising
summary: A premature revolt of the Jaca garrison in Aragon was quickly subdued; commanders Captains Fermin Galan and Garcia Hernandez were executed by firing squads, and the broader Republican rising failed.

citation.quote: According to the Republican version, it was unexpectedly pushed back to December 12 by a premature revolt of the Jaca garrison in Aragon. The rebellious troops were quickly subdued and their two commanders, Captains Fermin Galan and Garcia Hernandez, executed by firing squads.

title: Memorias de Congreso Extraordinario de la CNT published
summary: The record of the special CNT congress was published in Barcelona in 1931 as Memorias de Congreso Extraordinario de la C.N.T., containing a remarkable account of the confederation's vicissitudes.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: *Memorias de Congreso Extraordinario de la C.N.T. celebrado en Madrid los Dias 11 al 16 de \]unio de 1931* (Barcelona, 1931), contains a remarkable account of the vicissitudes of the confederation during the closing years of the dictatorship.

title: Berenguer resigns
summary: Faced by massive public hostility, Berenguer resigned his office; a nonpolitical government headed by Admiral Aznar took over.

citation.quote: In February 1931, Berenguer, faced by massive public hostility, resigned his office.

title: CNT workers vote for Republican bloc
summary: Many syndicalist (CNT) workers joined Socialist workers in voting for the Republican bloc, helping to oust the monarchy and bring in the Second Republic.

citation.quote: In April 1931 many syndicalist workers joined with Socialist workers in voting for the Republican bloc.

title: Spanish municipal elections; Republicans win
summary: Spain went to the polls in municipal elections, with the Republican-Socialist coalition winning a stunning victory. Two days later Alfonso departed hastily for Marseilles.

citation.quote: On April 12, 1931, Spain went to the polls. By evening, the earliest returns left no doubt that the Republican-Socialist coalition had won a stunning victory. Two days later, Alfonso departed hastily for Marseilles while the avenues of Spain's major cities were swollen with jubilant crowds waving Republican flags.

title: Cardinal Segura's pastoral letter denouncing the Republic
summary: Cardinal Segura, the primate of Spain, issued a pastoral letter denouncing the new regime's 'anarchy' and thanking the king for preserving Spanish piety, provoking convent burnings days later.

citation.quote: Early in May 1931, Cardinal Segura, the primate of Spain, issued a pastoral letter sharply denouncing the "anarchy" and "grave commotion" that the new regime had introduced.

title: Convent burnings in Madrid and other cities
summary: Three days after Cardinal Segura's pastoral letter, scuffles between Monarchists and anti-Monarchists in Madrid led to six convents being set aflame; the burnings spread to Malaga, Seville, Alicante and other cities.

citation.quote: As luck would have it, three days later scuffles broke out between Monarchists and anti-Monarchists in Madrid; a crowd, angered by anti-Monarchist rumors, gathered before the Ministry of Interior and in the morning hours six convents in the capital were set aflame. The convent burnings spread from Madrid to Malaga, Seville, Alicante, and other cities.

title: CNT Extraordinary National Congress at Madrid Conservatory
summary: The 418 delegates to the CNT's Extraordinary National Congress convened at the Madrid Conservatory; it was the first national congress since 1919 and would be the last until the eve of the Civil War. CNT claimed over half a million members in 511 syndicates.

citation.quote: When the 418 delegates to the congress convened at the Madrid Conservatory on June 11, the CNT could claim a membership of over a half million, organized into 511 syndicates.

title: Special CNT congress in Madrid
summary: The CNT held a special extraordinary congress in Madrid from June 11 to 16, 1931, whose record was later published as Memorias de Congreso Extraordinario de la C.N.T.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: The record of the special CNT congress in 1931, *Memorias de Congreso Extraordinario de la C.N.T. celebrado en Madrid los Dias 11 al 16 de \]unio de 1931* (Barcelona, 1931), contains a remarkable account of the vicissitudes of the confederation during the closing years of the dictatorship.

title: CNT telephone workers strike begins
summary: Thousands of CNT telephone workers walked off their jobs, confronting the Republic with a major test. The strike achieved its greatest successes in Barcelona and Seville and degenerated into guerrilla actions between CNT saboteurs and government forces; some 2,000 strikers were arrested.

citation.quote: On July 4, thousands of CNT telephone workers walked off their jobs, confronting the government with what Peirats calls "un 'test'" of the republic's intentions.

title: Seville general strike erupts
summary: A general strike broke out in Seville stemming from the telephone workers' walkout, with serious street fighting and Communist support. After nine days under martial law the strike ended; the CNT headquarters was reduced to shambles by artillery fire and 40 were killed, 200 wounded.

citation.quote: Scarcely had this conspiracy faded from public attention when, on July 20, a general strike broke out in Seville and serious fighting erupted in the streets.

title: Manifesto of the Thirty (Treintistas)
summary: Thirty CNT moderates signed a vigorous statement denouncing the FAI's conspiratorial, ultra-revolutionary policies, warning they would lead to 'Republican fascism.' The manifesto led to the moderates being isolated within the CNT.

citation.quote: The tensions within the organization finally came to a head when in August 1931, thirty moderates signed a vigorous statement denouncing the conspiratorial, ultra-revolutionary policies of the FAI.

title: FAI gains control of Barcelona key syndicates
summary: By September 1931 the FAI, riding a rank-and-file wave of revolutionary enthusiasm, had gained control of Barcelona's key syndicates.

citation.quote: By September 1931 the FAI, riding on a rank-and-file wave of revolutionary enthusiasm, had gained control of Barcelona's key syndicates

title: Faistas seize Solidaridad Obrera editorial board
summary: Faistas and hard-line Anarchosyndicalists unseated the moderate editorial board of Solidaridad Obrera and assumed control of the CNT newspaper.

citation.quote: a month later, in October, faistas and hard-line Anarchosyndicalists unseated the moderate editorial board of Solidaridad Obrera and assumed control of the newspaper.

title: UGT membership triples to nearly 960,000
summary: Eight months after the Republic was proclaimed, the UGT had grown to 4,041 local sections and nearly 960,000 members, tripling its membership in two years.

citation.quote: By December 1931, eight months after the republic was proclaimed, the union could boast of 4,041 local sections and nearly 960,000 members, a tripling of membership in only two years.

title: Orts-Ramos publishes Francisco Ferrer biography
summary: A. and C. Orts-Ramos's Francisco Ferrer—Apostal de la Razon is published in Barcelona, a personal and intellectual biography.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: A. and C. Orts-Ramos's *Francisco Ferrer—Apostal de la Razon* (Barcelona, 1932) is a highly informative personal and intellectual biography.

title: Alto Llobregat insurrection
summary: The first of the FAI insurrections began in the Catalan mining comarcal of the Alto Llobregat. In Figols, Manresa, Berga, Sallent and other towns, miners seized town halls, raised CNT flags, and declared comunismo libertario; the revolt was crushed in five days.

citation.quote: The first of these insurrections began on January 18, 1932, in the Catalan mining comarcal of the Alto Llobregat. In Figols, Manresa, Berga, Salient, and other towns, miners and other workers seized town halls, raised the black-and-red flags of the CNT, and declared comunismo libertario.

title: Durruti and Ascaso deported after Alto Llobregat
summary: A month after the Alto Llobregat uprising, over a hundred militants, including Durruti and Francisco Ascaso, were deported to Spanish West Africa and the Canary Islands. Durruti would not be released until the following autumn.

citation.quote: A month later, over a hundred militants, including Durruti and Francisco Ascaso, were deported to Spanish West Africa and the Canary Islands. Durruti was not to be released until the following autumn.

title: Pestana founds the Syndicalist Party
summary: Parting from his moderate comrades, Angel Pestana founded his own Syndicalist Party, which would send two deputies to the Cortes in the 1936 elections.

citation.quote: Finally, in April 1932, Pestana, parting even from his moderate comrades, was to found his own Syndicalist Party, which actually sent two deputies to the Cortes in the elections of 1936.

title: Catalan regional plenum of Sabadell — CNT split
summary: At the Catalan regional plenum of Sabadell, the walkout of treintista-influenced syndicates initiated an outright split that extended from Catalonia through the Levant to Andalusia and Asturias, forming the Sindicatos de Oposicion.

citation.quote: At the Catalan regional plenum of Sabadell in April 1932, the walkout of treintista-influenced syndicates initiated an outright split that extended from Catalonia, through the Levant, to Andalusia and Asturias.

title: UGT membership reaches 1,050,000
summary: By July 1932 UGT figures had soared to almost 5,107 local sections and 1,050,000 members.

citation.quote: In July 1932, these figures had soared to almost 5,107 and 1,050,000 respectively.

title: Sanjurjo's failed military rising in Seville
summary: General Sanjurjo, former commander of the Civil Guard, declared against the 'illegitimate Cortes' in a poorly planned, indecisive rising in Seville. He was easily defeated and the Azaña regime emerged with prestige.

citation.quote: On August 10, General Sanjurjo, the erstwhile commander of the Civil Guard, declared against the "illegitimate Cortes" in a poorly planned, indecisive rising in Seville.

title: Agrarian Statute passed
summary: The Second Republic passed its Agrarian Statute, intended to initiate sweeping land redistribution, but it was hobbled by inadequate funds and procrastination and changed little for the rural poor.

citation.quote: The republic's famous Agrarian Statute of September 1932, ostensibly designed to initiate a sweeping land redistribution program, hardly rates serious attention.

title: Pestana's Lo que Aprendi en la Vida published
summary: Angel Pestana's Lo que Aprendi en la Vida was published in Madrid, providing a personal account contributing to the history of the strike movement.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: Angel Pestana's *Lo que Aprendi en la Vida* (Madrid, 1933)

title: Buenacasa's La C.N.T., los Treinta y la F.A.I. published
summary: Buenacasa's La C.N.T., los Treinta y la F.A.I. is published in Barcelona, presenting the FAI outlook in the dispute with CNT moderates.

citation.quote: Buenacasa's *La C.N.T., los Treinta y la F.A.I.* (Barcelona, 1933) presents the outlook of the FAI in the dispute with the CNT moderates by a leader who is by no means a spokesman for its most extreme wing.

title: Casas Viejas massacre
summary: In Casas Viejas near Jerez de la Frontera, an Anarchist 'dynasty' led by Seisdedos ('Six Fingers') proclaimed comunismo libertario and was besieged by Civil and Assault Guards. The hut where Seisdedos and his family sheltered was burned; about fourteen prisoners were shot in cold blood by Captain Rojas's platoon.

citation.quote: In January 1933, almost a year to the day after the Alto Llobregat events, the FAI dragged the CNT into another insurrectionary adventure.

title: FAI insurrection in Barcelona
summary: The FAI-led insurrection began with assaults by Anarchist action groups and Cadres of Defense on Barcelona's military barracks. The attacks were repelled with bloodshed and arrests; uprisings also occurred in Tarassa, Sardanola, Ripollet, Lleida, Valencia province, and Andalusia. Garcia Oliver and most members of the FAI's Peninsular Committee were arrested.

citation.quote: The insurrection began on January 8 with assaults by Anarchist action groups and Cadres of Defense on Barcelona's military barracks.

title: Cardona potash miners strike
summary: In mid-April 1933 the potash miners walked out in Cardona, followed days later by Barcelona building workers and then dock workers, kicking off a massive CNT strike wave that culminated in a general strike across Catalonia and the country.

citation.quote: In mid-April the potash miners walked out in Cardona, followed a few days later by the building workers in Barcelona. Shortly afterward, the dock workers went on strike.

title: FNTT membership reaches 451,000
summary: By June 1933 the FNTT membership had soared to 451,000, accounting for 40 percent of the UGT's total membership.

citation.quote: but by June 1933 this figure had soared to 451,000, accounting for 40 percent of the UGT's total membership.

title: Tribunal of Constitutional Guarantees overturns Catalan ley de cultivos
summary: In June 1933 the Tribunal of Constitutional Guarantees overturned the Catalan ley de cultivos, a Generalitat law that would have empowered long-tenured vineyard tenants to acquire title to their land.

citation.quote: Yet in June 1933, even this circumscribed piece of legislation was so antithetical to Madrid's conservative agrarian policies that it was overturned by the Tribunal of Constitutional Guarantees, the Spanish equivalent of the American Supreme Court.

title: 60,000 cenetistas rally in Barcelona bull ring
summary: The CNT's campaign to release imprisoned CNT-FAI militants (about 9,000) peaked with a monster rally of 60,000 cenetistas in Barcelona's bull ring, with 'amnesty' appearing on posters and banners throughout.

citation.quote: In September, this movement reached its peak with a monster rally of 60,000 cenetistas in Barcelona's huge bull ring.

title: FAI plenum in Madrid calls for post-election uprising
summary: At a FAI plenum held in Madrid during the last days of October 1933, delegates pressed the need to prepare for an uprising after the elections, resolving that the upsurge of all effectives into Social Revolution should answer any rightist victory.

citation.quote: At a FAI plenum held in Madrid during the last days of October, the delegates pressed the need to prepare for an uprising after the elections.

title: CNT plenum debates uprising against new Cortes
summary: At a plenum of regional confederations held in October, most delegates probably opposed an uprising but not openly; only a few delegations, most notably the Aragonese, pressed for action.

citation.quote: At a plenum of regional confederations held in October, most of the delegates probably opposed an uprising, "but not openly," as A.M. Lehning reported. Only a few delegations, most notably the Aragonese, pressed for an uprising.

title: Pestana calls for Alianza Obrera entente of UGT and CNT
summary: The slogan of an Alianza Obrera was raised as early as October 1933, when Pestana, on behalf of the Treintistas, spelled out the need for an entente of the UGT and CNT to stop fascism in Spain.

citation.quote: The slogan, in fact, had been raised as early as October 1933, when Pestana, on behalf of the Treintistas, spelled out the need for an "entente," a "coalition" of the UGT and CNT to stop fascism in Spain.

title: Durruti speech at Barcelona anti-electoral rally
summary: At an immense anti-electoral rally of 75,000 workers in Barcelona's bull ring, Durruti called out the Republic for jailing 9,000 working men, culminating the CNT-FAI 'No Votad' campaign before the November elections.

citation.quote: On November 5, at an immense anti-electoral rally of 75,000 workers in the Barcelona bull ring, Durruti shouted: "Workers, you who voted yesterday without considering the consequences: if they told you that the Republic was going to jail 9,000 working men, would you have voted?"

title: Right-wing victory in Spanish parliamentary elections
summary: Parliamentary elections delivered an overwhelming victory to the right and ushered in what the Spanish labor movement called el bienio negro, the two black years. The CEDA emerged as the largest party with 110 seats, followed by Lerroux's Radicals with 100.

citation.quote: The parliamentary elections of November 19, 1933, brought an overwhelming victory to the right and ushered in what the Spanish labor movement was to call el bienio negro—the two black years.

title: Soldiers under Sergeant Sopena join uprising in Villanueva de Serena
summary: A noteworthy break in the faista pattern occurred at Villanueva de Serena, where a group of soldiers under a Sergeant Sopena joined the insurrection. Within four days the entire insurrectionary movement was crushed.

citation.quote: Perhaps the most noteworthy break in the faista pattern of ill-prepared rising, sporadic conflicts, short-lived localized victories, and swift triumphs by the army occurred in Villanueva de Serena, where a group of soldiers under a Sergeant Sopena joined the insurrection.

title: Death of Colonel Macia, founder of the Esquerra
