summary: Colonel Macia, founder of the Esquerra and an unequivocal Catalan separatist, died in December 1933. Under Companys the party began to orient itself toward autonomy within the Spanish republic.

citation.quote: Under Companys, the Esquerra had begun to abandon the unequivocally separatist policies of its founder, Colonel Macia (who died in December 1933) and was in the process of orienting itself toward autonomy within the Spanish republic.

title: Anarchosyndicalist December uprising begins
summary: The CNT-FAI uprising was timed for December 8, 1933, the opening day of the new Cortes. In Barcelona it began with a spectacular prison break of militants who had tunneled their way out following the Tarassa events.

citation.quote: The uprising was timed for December 8, 1933, the opening day of the new Cortes. In Barcelona, it began with a spectacular prison break in which many militants who had been imprisoned for participating in the Tarassa events tunneled their way to freedom.

title: Mass arrest of Aragonese anarchist leaders in Saragossa
summary: On the night of the eighth, nearly a hundred militants—including Durruti, Puente, and Mera—were arrested in Saragossa where they had gone to organize the insurrection.

citation.quote: Again, the government acted decisively to forestall an uprising; on the night of the eighth, nearly a hundred militants (including Durruti, Puente, and Mera) were arrested.

title: Only 12,000 families settled under Agrarian Statute
summary: Two years after the Agrarian Statute's passage, fewer than 12,000 families had received land, leaving the Spanish countryside more rebellious than before.

citation.quote: By late 1934, two years after the statute's passage, little more than 12,000 families had received land.

title: Mella's Ensayos y Conferencias published in Gijon
summary: Ricardo Mella's Ensayos y Conferencias is published in Gijon as Volume Two of his Obras Completas.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Ricardo Mella's *Ideario* (Gijon, 1926) and *Ensayos y Conferencias* (Gijon, 1934), both of which constitute Volumes One and Two respectively

title: Saragossa general strike of nearly five weeks
summary: In April the Aragonese city was paralyzed by one of the most extraordinary general strikes in Spanish labor history—a strike lasting nearly five weeks, occasioned by police brutality after a bomb explosion at police headquarters.

citation.quote: In April the Aragonese city was paralyzed by one of the most extraordinary general strikes to occur in the stormy history of the Spanish labor movement—a strike lasting nearly five weeks whose spirit of self-sacrifice, solidarity, and tenacity reached heroic proportions.

title: Barcelona caravan brings 13,000 strikers' children to Catalonia
summary: During the Saragossa strike the Barcelona proletariat under Durruti organized a caravan to bring the children of strikers to Catalonia. Fleets of taxis conveyed 13,000 children to cenetista families who pledged to care for them.

citation.quote: To lighten the burden of the Saragossa workers, the Barcelona proletariat under Durruti organized a spectacular caravan to bring the children of the strikers to Catalonia. Fleets of taxis were mobilized to convey 13,000 children to the thousands of cenetista families which had pledged to care for them.

title: CNT plenum permits local Alianza Obrera agreements with UGT
summary: At a June plenum of regional confederations, the CNT's blanket opposition to the Alianza Obrera was modified to allow agreements with the UGT on a local level, ratifying the Asturian CNT's earlier independent alliance.

citation.quote: Although the CNT as a whole retained its hostility toward the alliance, at a June plenum of regional confederations its opposition was modified to allow for agreements with the UGT on a local level.

title: Uprising of the Asturian miners
summary: Bookchin recalls vividly the uprising of the Asturian miners, a key precursor to the Spanish Civil War.

citation.quote: As one who had lived through the Spanish Civil War period, indeed, who vividly recalled the uprising of the Asturian miners in October 1934,1 thought it all the more necessary to correct the false image that, if it existed in my mind, almost certainly existed in the minds of my less politically involved contemporaries.

title: Companys declares Catalan State within Spanish Federal Republic
summary: With his back to the wall amid pressure from Rabassaires and escamots, Companys went through the public motions of declaring a Catalan State within the Federal Spanish Republic and barricaded himself in the Generalitat, surrendering at dawn.

citation.quote: Companys, his back to the wall, went through the public motions of declaring a "Catalan State within the Federal Spanish Republic" (a far cry from the outright independence the crowds were clamoring for) and quickly barricaded himself inside the Generalitat building, awaiting rescue by the central government's troops.

title: Death penalty restored in Spain
summary: The death penalty was restored in Spain in October 1934, becoming a focus of CNT protest meetings in early 1936.

citation.quote: the CNT boomed to the surface all over Spain with meetings protesting against fascism, against the death penalty (restored in October 1934)

title: CEDA topples Radical government with ministerial demand
summary: With the convening of the Cortes on October 1, the CEDA, demanding seats in the cabinet, dramatically toppled the Radical government. Alcala Zamora had no choice but to call on Lerroux to form a second cabinet granting the CEDA three ministries.

citation.quote: With the convening of the Cortes on October 1, the CEDA, demanding seats in the cabinet, dramatically toppled the Radical government. Despite his profound hostility to Gil Robles, President Alcala Zamora had no choice but to accede to the CEDA's demands.

title: Asturian miners launch general strike and attack Civil Guard barracks
summary: On the night of October 4, to the sound of sirens in the valley towns along the Aller and Nalon rivers, the Asturian miners began their strike with attacks on Civil Guard and Assault Guard barracks.

citation.quote: On the night of October 4, to the sound of sirens in the valley towns along the Aller and Nalon rivers, the miners began their strike with attacks on Civil Guard and Assault Guard barracks.

title: Asturian Insurrection runs roughly two weeks
summary: The Asturian insurrection lasted some two weeks, roughly from October 5 to October 18. Franco directed mercenary Moorish Regulares and the Foreign Legion to crush it, killing thousands and filling Spanish jails with 30–40,000 prisoners.

citation.quote: The Asturian insurrection lasted some two weeks, roughly from October 5 to October 18. During this brief period, the miners had behaved with exemplary dignity and moral rectitude.

title: Miners' column of 8,000 attacks Oviedo
summary: On October 6 the miners attacked Oviedo, the provincial capital. A column of 8,000 occupied all of the city except the Pelago and Santa Clara barracks, where government troops continued to hold out.

citation.quote: Following the surrender of the Civil and Assault Guards, they proceeded to occupy towns along the route to Oviedo, the provincial capital of Asturias, until on October 6 they attacked the city itself. In fact at this time a miners' column of 8,000... began to occupy all of Oviedo with the exception of the Pelago and Santa Clara barracks...

title: Oviedo Committee denies arms to Anarchist delegates from coastal seaports
summary: When Anarchist delegates from Aviles and Gijon arrived in Oviedo on October 7 pleading for arms to resist imminent government landings, their requests were totally ignored by Socialists and Communists who mistrusted them.

citation.quote: When Anarchist delegates from the seaports arrived in Oviedo on October 7, pleading for arms to resist the imminent landings of government troops, their requests were totally ignored by Socialists and Communists who, as Jackson notes, "clearly mistrusted them...."

title: CEDA withdraws from government over commuted Asturian sentences
summary: After Alcala Zamora and Lerroux commuted the death sentences of innocent Socialists targeted by Gil Robles, the CEDA at the end of March withdrew from the government, provoking another ministerial crisis.

citation.quote: Their sentences were commuted, whereupon the CEDA at the end of March withdrew from the government, provoking another ministerial crisis.

title: CNT plenum invites Opposition Syndicates to next congress
summary: A national plenum of Regional Confederations invited the Opposition Syndicates to participate in the next CNT national congress, with voice but not vote.

citation.quote: As early as May 1935, a national plenum of Regional Confederations had invited the Opposition Syndicates to participate in the next national congress of the CNT, albeit with a voice and not a vote.

title: Peiro endorses voting against fascists
summary: Moderate Anarchosyndicalist Juan Peiro wrote that if an electoral class front appeared against the governing fascists, he would for the first time in his life vote.

citation.quote: It took considerable courage for a moderate Anarchosyndicalist such as Juan Peiro to write in September 1935: “I have said, and I repeat it here, that if an electoral class front should appear against the fascists who now govern us, I, for the first time in my life, would vote....”

title: Lerroux forced to step down amid scandals
summary: By December, Lerroux was forced to step down after Radicals became involved in shady scandals over gambling licenses and army supply contracts. His tax bill to raise inheritance taxes from 1 to 3.5 percent triggered the CEDA's final withdrawal.

citation.quote: By December, Lerroux was forced to step down; indeed, the entire Radical Party had become a useless and discredited anachronism.

title: Alcala Zamora hands government to caretaker Portela Valladares
summary: On December 14, Alcala Zamora turned the government over to caretaker prime minister Manuel Portela Valladares. Within three weeks Portela lifted press censorship and dissolved the Cortes, announcing elections for February 16, 1936.

citation.quote: On December 14, to the utter astonishment of the right, Alcala, Zamora turned the government over to a caretaker prime minister, Manuel Portela Yalladares, formerly Lerroux's minister of interior and an opponent of Gil Robles's attempts to transfer the Civil Guards to the Ministry of War.

title: CNT reaches one million members on eve of Spanish Civil War
summary: On the eve of the Spanish Civil War, approximately a million people were members of the Anarchosyndicalist CNT, an immense following given Spain's population of twenty-four million.

citation.quote: In 1936, on the eve of the Spanish Civil War, approximately a million people were members of the Anarchosyndicalist CNT (Confederation National del Trabajo, or National Confederation of Labor)—an immense following if one bears in mind that the Spanish population numbered only twenty-four million.

title: Franco's march toward Madrid
summary: The slaughter and terror following Franco's march toward Madrid in the late summer of 1936 brought to the surface the latent weaknesses of the classical workers' movement.

citation.quote: The slaughter and terror that followed in the wake of Franco's march toward Madrid in the late summer of 1936 and the physical hemorrhage that claimed so many lives in the long course of the Civil War produced a spiritual hemorrhage as well, bringing to the surface all the latent weaknesses of the classical workers' movement as such, both Anarchist and Socialist.

title: Franco recruits northern peasant infantry
summary: Bookchin notes that the small landowners of the mountains of Navarre and nearby reactionary northern regions supplied General Franco with the most enthusiastic domestic masses for his infantry in 1936.

citation.chapter: Chapter Two: The Topography of Revolution
citation.quote: nevertheless, it was from the small landowners of the mountains of Navarre and nearby areas that General Franco was to recruit the most enthusiastic domestic masses for his infantry in 1936.

title: BOC and Izquierda Comunista merge to form POUM
summary: The Bloc Obrer i Camperol and Izquierda Comunista merged to form the POUM (Workers' Party of Marxist Unification), which became a principal target of Stalinist repression during the Civil War.

citation.quote: In 1936, the two organizations merged to form the POUM—the Partido Obrero de Unification Marxista (Workers' Party of Marxist Unification)—a sizable organization which became the principal target of Stalinist abuse and repression during the Civil War years.

title: Santillan warns communism requires abundance
summary: In the spring of 1936, shortly before the military rebellion, Abad de Santillan warned in After the Revolution that "Communism will be the result of abundance, without which it will remain only an ideal."

citation.quote: "Communism will be the result of abundance," Santillan had warned in the spring of 1936, "without which it will remain only an ideal."

title: Villar's El Anarquismo y la Insurreccion de Asturias published
summary: Manuel Villar's El Anarquismo y la Insurrection de Asturias is published in Buenos Aires, presenting the Anarchist version of the Asturian uprising.

citation.quote: Manuel Villar's *El Anarquismo y la Insurrection de Asturias* (Buenos Aires, 1936) presents the Anarchist version of the Asturian uprising.

title: Santillan's El Organismo Economico de la Revolucion published
summary: Diego Abad de Santillan's El Organismo Eamomico de la Revolution is published in Barcelona, a reflective theoretical work and guide to social reconstruction.

citation.quote: My choice of Diego Abad de Santillan's *El Organismo Eamomico de la Revolution* (Barcelona, 1936), translated into English under the title, *After the Revolution* (New York, 1937), as the most useful of the two works was guided by the need for a more discursive treatment.

title: Popular Front pact formally established
summary: A pact to form the Popular Front was established between the Socialist Party, UGT, Left Republicans, Republican Union, Socialist Youth, Pestana's Syndicalist Party, Communist Party, and POUM.

citation.quote: In mid-January 1936, a pact to form a Popular Front was finally established by the Socialist Party, the UGT, the Left Republicans and their allies of-the Republican Union, the Socialist Youth, Pestana’s Syndicalist Party, the Communist Party, and surprisingly, the newly formed POUM

title: Catalan Regional Committee conference debates elections
summary: At a conference of the Catalan Regional Committee, angry delegates charged the Regional Committee with a temporizing attitude toward the upcoming elections.

citation.quote: On January 25, 1936, at a conference of the Catalan Regional Committee, angry delegates bluntly charged the Regional Committee with a temporizing attitude toward the forthcoming elections.

title: FAI peninsular plenum ratifies electoral position
summary: A peninsular plenum of the FAI held in Barcelona ratified the Catalan regional conference's electoral position, reaffirming abstention only nominally while quietly tolerating voting.

citation.quote: A peninsular plenum of the FAI, held in Barcelona on January 30 and February 1, ratified the electoral position of the Catalan regional conference.

title: Popular Front coalition takes power in Spain
summary: Caballero, released from prison, became the leader of the Socialist left and an architect of the Popular Front coalition that took power in February 1936.

citation.quote: Soon to be released from prison, he became the indubitable leader of the Socialist left and another architect of the “Popular Front” coalition that was to take power in February 1936.

title: CNT manifesto warns of impending military coup
summary: The CNT issued a prophetic manifesto warning of a likely right-wing military coup centered in Morocco, pledging to fight fascism even without supporting the Republic.

citation.quote: As early as February 14, the CNT had issued a prophetic manifesto warning that day by day, “the suspicion grows that right-wing elements are ready to provoke a military coup. Morocco appears to be the focal point of the conspiracy.

title: National elections announced ending el bienio negro
summary: Portela dissolved the Cortes and announced national elections for February 16, 1936. El bienio negro—the two black years of reactionary rule, repression, and the drift toward a corporative state—had come to an end.

citation.quote: At the same time, he dissolved the Cortes and announced national elections for February 16, 1936. El brenio negro, the two black years of reactionary rule, repression, and the drift toward a corporative state, had come to an end.

title: Popular Front wins Spanish elections
summary: The February 1936 elections brought the Popular Front parties to power by a margin of some 700,000 votes, winning 271 seats and an absolute majority in the Cortes.

citation.quote: The elections of February 1936 brought the Popular Front parties to power by a margin of some 700,000 votes. Of 271 seats acquired by the coalition, a number which constituted an absolute majority in the Cortes, the Republicans (including Martinez Barrio’s Republican Union as well as Azana’s *Izquierda)* were given 117 seats, the Socialists 90, and the Communists 16.

title: CNT National Committee invites Treintistas to Saragossa congress
summary: The National Committee of the CNT invited former Treintistas to attend the upcoming Confederation congress at Saragossa on May 1st, bringing the unity question to a head.

citation.quote: The problem of confederal unity came to a head in March 1936, when the National Committee of the CNT invited former *Treintistas* to attend the forthcoming congress of the Confederation at Saragossa on May 1<sup>st</sup>.

title: Massive land seizures across Spain
summary: Following the Popular Front victory, some 250,000 hectares were taken over by squatters in March, with major land seizures continuing through spring.

citation.quote: In March, some 250,000 hectares were taken over by squatters, about 150,000 in April, and more than 90,000 in May and June together.

title: UGT and CNT steel workers strike
summary: In late March 1936, both UGT and CNT steel workers left their foundries as part of the strike wave that swept Spain after the Popular Front victory.

citation.quote: In late March, both UGT and CNT steel workers left their foundries; in mid-April the CNT initiated a general strike in Madrid that gained the support of the UGT workers, to be followed in early June by still another strike, this time of construction and elevator workers.

title: Generals meet secretly in Madrid to plan revolt
summary: As early as March 1936, the generals and politicians who would stage the military uprising of July 17 met secretly in Madrid to formulate their plans.

citation.quote: As early as March, scarcely more than a few weeks after the Popular Front had come to power, the generals and politicians who were to stage the military uprising of July 17 met secretly in Madrid to formulate their plans.

title: CNT general strike in Madrid
summary: In mid-April 1936, the CNT initiated a general strike in Madrid that gained the support of UGT workers.

citation.quote: in mid-April the CNT initiated a general strike in Madrid that gained the support of the UGT workers, to be followed in early June by still another strike, this time of construction and elevator workers.

title: Dobby publishes 'Agrarian Problems in Spain'
summary: E.H.G. Dobby's article 'Agrarian Problems in Spain' appears in the Geographical Review of the American Geographical Society.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: see "Agrarian Problems in Spain" by E.H.G. Dobby, *Geographical Review of the American Geographical Society* April, 1936).

title: Saragossa congress of the CNT
summary: The CNT holds its Saragossa congress, whose record is later republished by Ediciones "CNT" as El Congreso Confederal de Zaragoza.

citation.quote: The record of the Saragossa congress of May 1936 has been republished by Ediciones "CNT" as part of its series *Prolegomenos de la Revolution de Julio en Espana* under the title, *El Congreso Confederal de Zaragoza* (n.p., 1955).

title: CNT national congress at Saragossa opens
summary: Nearly 650 delegates representing 982 syndicates with 550,000 members convened at Iris Park in Saragossa for the CNT national congress, lasting ten days and readmitting the Opposition Syndicates.

citation.quote: On the first day of the month, nearly 650 delegates, representing 982 syndicates with a membership of 550,000, convened at the Iris Park. This congress, lasting ten days, was to become known as one of the most memorable meetings in the history of the CNT.

title: Prieto predicts Franco as future dictator
summary: Indalecio Prieto warned of a military revolt and singled out Franco as the most likely candidate for the dictator of Spain.

citation.quote: On May 1<sup>st</sup>, Prieto with uncanny prescience not only had warned of a military revolt but had singled out Franco as the most likely candidate for the dictator of Spain.

title: Madrid construction and elevator workers strike
summary: In June 1936, 40,000 construction workers and 30,000 electricians and elevator repairmen from both CNT and UGT went out on strike in Madrid, leading to violent clashes.

citation.quote: The test of Caballero’s intentions came in June 1936, when 40,000 construction workers and 30,000 electricians and elevator repairmen, both groups drawn from the CNT and UGT, went out on strike in Madrid.

title: Prieto wins Socialist Party elections over Caballero
summary: At Socialist Party elections on June 30, Prieto's supporters received a larger proportion of votes than Caballero's, showing the party's diehards favored moderation.

citation.quote: At the party elections of June 30, Prieto’s supporters received a larger proportion of the votes than Caballero’s.

title: Great popular uprising of July 1936
summary: The great popular uprising of July 1936, especially in the Anarchist centers of Spain, attempted to approximate the goal of direct, face-to-face control over everyday life.

citation.quote: The great popular uprising of July 1936, especially in the Anarchist centers of Spain, tried to approximate this goal.

title: Libertarian revolution makes Barcelona Spain's most revolutionary city
summary: In July 1936 the CNT and FAI, sufficiently independent from Socialists and POUM, made Barcelona the most revolutionary city in Spain — collectivizing industry and fostering communal land management more extensively than anywhere else.

citation.quote: In any case, the libertarian revolution of July 1936 seemed to have gathered to itself many of the noble qualities that were only partially developed in earlier uprisings of the worker's movement. In July 1936, the CNT and FAI were sufficiently independent as a workers' movement, certainly by comparison with the Socialists and POUM, to make Barcelona the most revolutionary city in Spain.

title: Falangists seize Radio Valencia
summary: A group of Falangists briefly seized the radio station of Valencia and broadcast a message announcing the Spanish Falange had taken possession of the transmitter by force of arms.

citation.quote: On July 11, a group of Falangists briefly seized the radio station of Valencia and broadcast the following message: “Radio Valencia. The Spanish Falange has taken possession of the transmitter by force of arms.

title: Calvo Sotelo assassinated in Madrid
summary: After a Socialist lieutenant of the Assault Guards was shot by Falangists, his comrades arrested right-wing parliamentary leader Calvo Sotelo and shot him, dumping his body in the Madrid cemetery.

citation.quote: The next day, on July 12, a Socialist lieutenant of the Assault Guards was shot to death by a group of Falangist gunmen. Within hours of the assassination, the victim’s angry comrades had decided upon a dramatic act of revenge. Arriving at Calvo Sotelo’s home in a police car, they “arrested” the right-wing parliamentary leader, drove off with him in their vehicle, and shot him

title: Generals declare pronunciamiento against Republic
summary: The day of the military uprising was pushed forward to July 17 to take advantage of the sensation produced by the assassinations, beginning the rebellion of the generals.

citation.quote: The day of the uprising was pushed forward to July 17 to take advantage of the sensation produced by the assassinations arid the commanders were placed in a state of readiness.

title: Barcelona workers defeat military rebellion
summary: Soldiers of the Barcelona garrison left their quarters to occupy the city but were met with barricades, snipers, and crowds; the libertarian social revolution had begun alongside the generals' uprising.

citation.quote: On July 18, the generals declared their *pronunciamiento* and, in the morning hours of the next day, soldiers of the Barcelona garrison, perhaps the largest in Spain, began to leave their quarters to occupy strategic centers of the city.

title: Solidaridad Obrera appeals during opening days of revolution
summary: Solidaridad Obrera publishes appeals from July 19 to July 23, 1936 covering the opening days of the revolution; these are collected in the concluding portion of Abel Paz's Paradigma de una Revolucion.

citation.quote: One of the most detailed accounts of the day-by-day conflict in Madrid and Barcelona appears in Abel Paz's *Paradigma de una Revolution* (n.p., n.d.), published by Ediciones *"ATT,"* the concluding portion of which contains appeals in *Solidaridad Obrera* from July 19 to July 23, 1936.

title: Killing of Antonio Martin
summary: Antonio Martin, one of the most daring of the 'Solidarios' who had handled the transit of arms through Puigcerda, was shot down by gunmen of the Spanish Communist Party.

citation.quote: In 1937, Martin was shot down by gunmen of the Spanish Communist Party.

title: Borkenau publishes The Spanish Cockpit
summary: Franz Borkenau's The Spanish Cockpit was published in London, a thoughtful book depicting Anarchism as a quasi-religious movement despite the author's Socialist convictions.

citation.quote: Franz Borkenau's The Spanish Cockpit (London, 1937), a very thoughtful book in its own right, also depicts Anarchi m as a quasi-religious movement one which, despite Borkenau's Socialist convictions, earns his esteem.

title: Carr publishes Michael Bakunin
summary: E.H. Carr's biography Michael Bakunin was published in London; Bookchin criticizes its account as steeped in malice toward its subject.

citation.quote: E.H. Carr, in his *Michael Bakunin* (London, 1937), has brought painstaking scholarship to the service of what are often scandalously trivial goals

title: Santillan's After the Revolution published in English
summary: Santillan's El Organismo Economico de la Revolucion appears in English translation as After the Revolution, published in New York.

citation.quote: Diego Abad de Santillan's *El Organismo Eamomico de la Revolution* (Barcelona, 1936), translated into English under the title, *After the Revolution* (New York, 1937)

title: May uprising in Barcelona
summary: Russell Blackwell fought with the Friends of Durruti in Barcelona during the May uprising in 1937.

citation.quote: Blackwell had fought with the Friends of Durruti in Barcelona during the May uprising in 1937.

title: Kaminski publishes Bakounine-La Vie d'un Révolutionnaire
summary: H.E. Kaminski's Bakounine-La Vie d'un Revolutionnaire, called by Bookchin the best biography to consult on Bakunin's activities, was published in Paris.

citation.quote: H.E. Kaminski's *Bakounine-La Vie d'un Revolutionnaire* (Paris, 1938) is the best biography to consult on Bakunin's activities

title: Marx and Engels's Revolution in Spain published
summary: A compilation of Marx and Engels's writings, Revolution in Spain, was published in New York, marred by Stalinist editing and Engels's diatribe 'The Bakuninists at Work.'

citation.quote: These articles are compiled in Marx and Engels's *Revolution in Spain* (New York, 1939), a book that is sadly marred not only by Stalinist editing but by Engels's vulgar interpretation of early syndicalism in a propaganda diatribe, "The Bakuninists at Work."

title: Santillan's Por que Perdimos la Guerra published
summary: Diego Abad de Santillan's Por que Perdimos la Guerra is published in Buenos Aires, with opening chapters tracing Spanish Anarchism from the First to the Second Republic and the July uprising.

citation.quote: Diego Abad de Santillan's *Por que Perdimos la Guerra* (Buenos Aires, 1940), the opening chapters of which provide an account of the development of the Spanish Anarchist movement from the First to the Second Republic and the outbreak of the July uprising.

title: Brenan publishes The Spanish Labyrinth
summary: Gerald Brenan's The Spanish Labyrinth was published in London, regarded by Bookchin as the finest and most moving account in English of the Spanish Anarchists.

citation.quote: Despite the minor errors that scholars have cited, Gerald Brenan's The Spanish Labyrinth (London, 1943) still remains the finest and most moving account in English of the Spanish Anarchists to date.

title: Rocker publishes Fermin Salvochea
summary: Rudolph Rocker's Fermin Salvochea appears as No. 1 in the Precursores de la Libertad series.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Rudolph Rocker's *Fermin Salvochea* in the *Precursores de la Libertad* series (No. 1,1945)

title: Ramos Oliveira publishes Politics, Economics and Men of Modern Spain
summary: A. Ramos Oliveira's Politics, Economics and Men of Modern Spain (1808–1946) is published in London, discussing the intertwining of agrarian and political interests.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: In *Politics, Economics and Men of Modem Spain (1808–1946)* (London, 1946), the intertwining of agrarian with political interests is discussed with much verve by A. Ramos Oliveira

title: Puente's El Comunismo Libertario republished in Toulouse
summary: Isaac Puente's El Comunismo Libertario — the basic theoretical document for the Saragossa congress's discussion of the future society — is republished at Toulouse.

citation.quote: The reader should also consult Isaac Puente's *El Comunismo Libertario* (republished at Toulouse, 1947), a work which formed the basic theoretical document for the congress's discussion of the future society.

title: Maximoff publishes The Political Philosophy of Bakunin
summary: Gregory Maximoff's mosaic of Bakunin's writings, The Political Philosophy of Bakunin, was published in Glencoe.

citation.quote: Gregory Maximoff's very unsatisfactory mosaic of Bakunin's writings, *The Political Philosophy of Bakunin* (Glencoe, 1953)

title: Richards's The Lessons of the Spanish Revolution published
summary: Vernon Richards's The Lessons of the Spanish Revolution is published in London, offering a sharp anarchist critique of the FAI and CNT's performance on the eve of the uprising and during the Civil War.

citation.quote: For a sharp criticism by an English Anarchist of the FAI and CNT's performance on the eve of the uprising as well as the Civil War, see Vernon Richard's *The Lessons of the Spanish Revolution* (London, 1953).

title: Largo Caballero's Mis Recuerdos published
summary: Francisco Largo Caballero's Mis Recuerdos was published in Mexico, providing a memoir relevant to the Spanish strike movement.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: Francisco Largo Caballero's *Mis Reciierdos* (Mexico, 1954).

title: Peirats's La C.N.T. en la Revolucion Espanola, Vol. I published
summary: The first volume of Peirats's La C.N.T. en la Revolution Espanola is published in Buenos Aires, collecting documents indispensable for understanding Anarchist activity from 1931 to 1936.

citation.quote: The opening chapters (I to IX) of Peirats's *La* C.N.T. *en la Revolution Espanola,* Vol. I (Buenos Aires, 1955), are indispensable for a knowledge of Anarchist activities during the period.

title: El Congreso Confederal de Zaragoza republished
summary: Ediciones "CNT" republishes the record of the May 1936 Saragossa congress as El Congreso Confederal de Zaragoza in its Prolegomenos series.

citation.quote: The record of the Saragossa congress of May 1936 has been republished by Ediciones "CNT" as part of its series *Prolegomenos de la Revolution de Julio en Espana* under the title, *El Congreso Confederal de Zaragoza* (n.p., 1955).

title: Comin Colomer publishes Historia del Anarquismo Espanol
summary: Eduardo Comin Colomer's two-volume Historia del Anarquismo Espanol 1836–1948 was published in Barcelona, a Francoist historia secreta drawn from police files.

citation.quote: Eduardo Comin Colomer's two-volume Historia del Anarquismo Espanol 1836–1948 (Barcelona 1956) is a typical Francoist historia secreta, written from an internal knowledge of the police files.

title: García Venero publishes Historia de las Internacionales en España
summary: Maximiano Garcia Venero's three-volume history of the Internationals in Spain was published in Madrid.

citation.quote: Maximiano Garcia Venero's three-volume *Historia de las Internationales en Espana* (Madrid, 1956–1958)

title: Brademas's Oxford dissertation completed
summary: John Brademas completed his unpublished doctoral dissertation "Revolution and Social Revolution: A Contribution to the History of the Anarcho-Syndicalist Movement in Spain, 1930-1937" at Oxford University.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: "Revolution and Social Revolution: A Contribution to the History of the Anarcho-Syndicalist Movement in Spain, 1930–1937" (Oxford University, unpublished, 1956).

title: Vicens Vives edits Historia Social y Económica de España y América
summary: The five-volume Historia Social y Economica de Espana y America, edited by Jaime Vicens Vives, was published in Barcelona.

citation.quote: the reader may care to consult the five-volume series *Historia Social y Economica de Espana y America,* edited by Jaime Vicens Vives (Barcelona, 1957–1959)

title: Memoria del Congreso celebrado en Barcelona 1918 published
summary: Ediciones "CNT" in Toulouse published the Memoria del Congreso celebrado en Barcelona, recording the 1918 Barcelona congress of the CNT.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: for the 1918 Barcelona congress see the *Memoria del Congreso celebrado en Barcelona los dias 28, 29 y 30 de Junio y 1 de Julio de 1918,* Ediciones "CNT" (Toulouse, 1957).

title: Vallina publishes biography of Salvochea
summary: Pedro Vallina's Cronica de un Revolucionario, a biography of Salvochea, is published in Paris.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: as is Pedro Vallina's biography of Salvochea, *Cronica de un Revolucionario* (Paris, 1958).

title: Ediciones CNT republishes El Proceso de La Mano Negra
summary: Ediciones 'CNT' republishes El Proceso de 'La Mano Negra' in Toulouse, an old collection of excerpts from statements of the accused.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Ediciones "CNT" has republished *El Proceso de "La Mano Negra"* (Toulouse, 1958)

title: Madariaga's Spain published
summary: Salvador de Madariaga's Spain is published in New York, offering a liberal interpretation of the period and of the conflicts between the UGT and CNT.

citation.quote: Salvador de Madariaga's *Spain* (New York, 1958) presents a liberal interpretation of the period and of the conflicts between the UGT and CNT.

title: Martí publishes Orígenes del Anarquismo en Barcelona
summary: Casimiro Marti's brief but masterful research on the origins of anarchism in Barcelona was published.

citation.quote: Casimiro Marti's *Origenes del Anarquismo en Barcelona* (Barcelona, 1959)

title: Coloma publishes La Revolución Internacionalista Alcoyana de 1873
summary: R. Coloma's widely cited account of the Alcoy uprising was published in Alicante, though Bookchin views it as biased against the Internationalists.

citation.quote: R. Coloma's widely cited *La Revolution Internacionalista Alcoyana de 1873* (Alicante, 1959), a work which seems to have acquired the reputation of an authoritative account on the Alcoy uprising

title: Hobsbawm publishes Primitive Rebels
summary: E.J. Hobsbawm's Primitive Rebels, containing an essay on Anarchist 'millenarianism,' is published in Manchester.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: E.J. Hobsbawm's essay on Anarchist "millenarianism" in *Primitive Rebels* (Manchester, 1959) is riddled by Marxian prejudgments on the "archaic" nature of Anarchism.

title: Hagnauer publishes L'Actualite de la Charte d'Amiens
summary: Roger Hagnauer's L'Actualite de la Charte d'Amiens is published in Paris, containing an account of the emergence of the French CGT.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Roger Hagnauer's *L'Actualite de la Charte d'Amiens* (Paris, 1959) contains a succinct account of the emergence of the French CGT

title: Congreso de Constitution de la CNT published
summary: Ediciones "CNT" in Toulouse published Congreso de Constitution de la Confederation National del Trabajo (CNT), a detailed account of the "Bellas Artes" congress of the CNT.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: For a detailed account of the "Bellas Artes" congress of the CNT, see the *Congreso de Constitution de la Confederation National del Trabajo (CNT),* Ediciones "CNT" (Toulouse, 1959)

title: Salvador Segui: su vida, su obra published
summary: Ediciones "Solidaridad Obrera" in Paris published a laudatory compilation of material on Salvador Segui by a variety of libertarian writers.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: A laudatory compilation of material on Salvador Segui by a variety of libertarian writers has been prepared by Ediciones *"Solidaridad Obrera"* under the title *Salvador Segui: su vida, su obra* (Paris, 1960).

title: García Venero publishes Historias de los Movimientos Sindicalistas Españoles
summary: Maximiano Garcia Venero's Historias de los Movimientos Sindicalistas Espanoles (1840–1933) was published in Madrid.

citation.quote: the same author's *Historias de los Movimientos Sindicalistas Espanoles (1840–1933)* (Madrid, 1961).

title: Kenny publishes A Spanish Tapestry
summary: Michael Kenny's A Spanish Tapestry is published in New York, depicting pueblo life.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: the reader should consult Michael Kenny's *A Spanish Tapestry* (New York, 1961)

title: Pitt-Rivers publishes The People of the Sierra
summary: J.S. Pitt-Rivers's study of an Andalusian mountain village, The People of the Sierra, is published in Chicago.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: J.S. Pitt-Rivers's sensitive study of an Andalusian mountain village, *The People of the Sierra* (Chicago, 1961).

title: Thomas's The Spanish Civil War published
summary: Hugh Thomas's The Spanish Civil War is published in New York; Bookchin sharply disputes its reputation as a definitive history of the conflict.

citation.quote: Hugh Thomas's *The Spanish Civil War* (New York, 1961)—a book that, for some curious reason, has acquired the reputation of being a "definitive" history of the conflict—is pretentious, superficial, and factually unreliable.

title: Richards's critique of Thomas appears in Anarchy
summary: Vernon Richards's essay "July 19, 1936: Republic or Revolution?" — a critique of Hugh Thomas's work — appears in Anarchy, No. 5.

citation.quote: the reader should consult Vernon Richards's "July 19, 1936: Republic or Revolution?" in *Anarchy,* No. 5 (July/1961), and Richards's introductory remarks to Gaston Leval's *Collectives in the Spanish Revolution* (London, 1975).

title: Hennessy publishes The Federal Republic in Spain
summary: C.A.M. Hennessy's The Federal Republic in Spain, with an extensive bibliography on Spanish Federalism, was published in Oxford.

citation.quote: Perhaps the best work I can recommend on Spanish Federalism is C.A.M. Hennessy's *The Federal Rebublic in Spain* (Oxford, 1962).

title: Peirats publishes Los Anarquistas en la Crisis Politica Espanola
summary: Jose Peirats's Los Anarquistas en la Crisis Politica Espanola was published in Buenos Aires, providing an introductory survey of early Spanish Anarchism.

citation.quote: The opening chapters of Cesar M. Lorenzo's Les Anarchistes Espagnols et le Pouvoir (Paris, 1969), Jose Peirats's Los Anarquistas en la Crisis Politica Espanola (Buenos Aires, 1964), and Manuel Buenacasa's El Movimiento Obrero Espanol (Paris, 1966) are the best I have found of such summaries.

title: La Souchère publishes An Explanation of Spain
summary: Elena de La Souchere's An Explanation of Spain, sympathetic to the libertarian spirit of the Spanish people, was published in New York.

citation.quote: I know of no book in English that is more deeply sympathetic to—or so ably conveys—the libertarian spirit of the Spanish people than Elena de La Souchere's *An Explanation of Spain* (New York, 1964).

title: Richards publishes Malatesta: His Life and Ideas
summary: Vernon Richards's Malatesta: His Life and Ideas, a biography and selection of Malatesta's writings, is published in London.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Vernon Richards under the title, *Malatesta: His Life and Ideas* (London, 1965).

title: Bacells's El Sindicalismo en Barcelona published
summary: Alberto Bacells's El Sindicalismo en Barcelona (1916-1923) was published in Barcelona, providing a detailed account of the strike movement during this period.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: Detailed accounts of the strike movement during this period appear in Alberto Bacells's *El Sindicalismo en Barcelona (1916–1923)* (Barcelona, 1965)

title: Jackson's The Spanish Republic and the Civil War published
summary: Gabriel Jackson's The Spanish Republic and the Civil War, 1931–1939 is published in Princeton, offering details often absent from general histories of the period.

citation.quote: Gabriel Jackson's *The Spanish Republic and the Civil War, 1931–1939* (Princeton, 1965) is very useful and provides many details that are not ordinarily available in general histories, although I share Noam Chomsky's criticisms of the book in his *The Cold War and the New Mandarins.*

title: Buenacasa publishes El Movimiento Obrero Espanol
summary: Manuel Buenacasa's El Movimiento Obrero Espanol was published in Paris, providing an introductory survey of early Spanish Anarchism.

citation.quote: The opening chapters of Cesar M. Lorenzo's Les Anarchistes Espagnols et le Pouvoir (Paris, 1969), Jose Peirats's Los Anarquistas en la Crisis Politica Espanola (Buenos Aires, 1964), and Manuel Buenacasa's El Movimiento Obrero Espanol (Paris, 1966) are the best I have found of such summaries.

title: Carr publishes Spain, 1808–1939
summary: Raymond Carr's Spain, 1808–1939, an informative work on Spanish political events, was published in Oxford.

citation.quote: Raymond Carr's *Spain, 1808–1939* (Oxford, 1966) is an eminently readable and highly informative work on political events.

title: Nomad publishes 'The Anarchist Tradition'
summary: Max Nomad's 'The Anarchist Tradition' appears in The Revolutionary Internationals, edited by M.M. Drachkovitch, published in Stanford.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: Max Nomad's "The Anarchist Tradition" (*The Revolutionary Internationals,* ed. M.M. Drachkovitch \[Stanford, 1966\]) provide valuable accounts of this split.

title: Tuchman publishes The Proud Tower
summary: Barbara W. Tuchman's The Proud Tower, containing an account of Anarchist terrorism, is published in New York.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: A dramatic, at times lurid, but not inaccurate account of Anarchist terrorism appears in Barbara W. Tuchman's *The Proud Tower* (New York, 1966).

title: Martin Maestre's Huelga General de 1917 published
summary: Jacinto Martin Maestre's Huelga General de 1917 was published in Madrid, providing a detailed account of the 1917 general strike.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: Jacinto Martin Maestre's *Huelga General de 1917* (Madrid, 1966)

title: Sanz's El Sindicalismo y La Politica published
summary: Ricardo Sanz published El Sindicalismo y La Politica in Toulouse, providing a personal account of the Solidarios and Nosotros affinity groups.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: Ricardo Sanz provides a personal account of the *Solidarios* and *Nosotros* affinity groups in *El Sindicalismo y La Politico* (Toulouse, 1966)

title: Gomez Casas publishes Historia del Anarcosindicalismo
summary: Juan Gomez Casas's Historia del Anarcosindicalismo was published in Madrid, providing an outline of major events in Spanish Anarchist history.

citation.quote: Juan Gomez Casa's Historia del Anarcosindicalismo (Madrid, 1968) is simply an outline of the major events in Spanish Anarchist history and does not live up to its grandiloquent title.

title: Abad de Santillan's Contribution a la Historia begins publication
summary: The first volume of Diego Abad de Santillan's series Contribution a la Historia del Movimiento Obrero Espanol was published in Madrid.

citation.quote: the reader might care to consult Diego Abad de Santillan's recent series, Contribution a la Historia del Movimiento Obrero Espanol, the first volume of which was published in Madrid in 1968.

title: Ullman publishes The Tragic Week
summary: Joan Connelly Ullman's The Tragic Week, an account of the Barcelona labor movement, is published in Cambridge.

citation.chapter: 3. From the International to the CNT (Chapters IV and Vll).
citation.quote: The finest account of the Barcelona labor movement during this decade is Joan Connelly Ullman's *The Tragic Week* (Cambridge, 1968)

title: Pestana's Informe de mi Estancia en la U.R.S.S. published
summary: Editorial ZYX in Madrid published Angel Pestana's report on his visit to Russia as Informe de mi Estancia en la U.R.S.S., along with the companion pamphlet Consideraciones y Juicios Acerca de la Tercera Internacional.

citation.chapter: 4. From the Early CNT to the Second Republic (Chapters VIII-IX)
citation.quote: Angel Pestana's report oi his visit to Russia has been published in recent years as two pamphlets by Editorial ZYX under the titles, *Informe de mi Estanda en la U.R.S.S.* (Madrid, 1968) and *Consideraciones y Juicios Acerca de la Tercera Internacional* (Madrid, 1968).

title: Lorenzo publishes Les Anarchistes Espagnols et le Pouvoir
